papers.abstract_en: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I-IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03161353 .

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Self-directed lifestyle interventions may improve access to weight loss care in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but effectiveness in routine practice is unknown. OBJECTIVE: Test whether a proactively delivered self-directed lifestyle intervention improves weight and sleep-related quality of life versus usual care. METHODS: POWER enrolled patients with OSA and body mass index of 30-45 kg/m2, recruited from Veteran Affairs (VA) sites nationwide, and randomized participants to a self-directed intervention based on the Diabetes Prevention Program with video-based sessions, readings, and regular coaching reminders or usual care. Co-primary outcomes were change in Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) and clinical weight in kilograms (kg) from baseline to 12 months post-randomization. Given two primary outcomes, we defined significance at p = 0.025. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: This trial randomized 696 participants. Mean age was 56.2 years (SD 12.2), with 19.7% identifying as female. Clinical weights at 12 months were available for 81.9% of intervention and 83.6% of control participants. Unadjusted weight declined 2.1 kg (SD 6.8) in intervention and 0.9 kg (SD 5.9) in control (adjusted between-group difference: -1.1 kg, 95%CI -2.0, -0.1; p = 0.037). FOSQ measures were available at 12 months for 78.2% of intervention and 90.5% of control participants. From baseline to 12 months, unadjusted FOSQ improved 1.4 (SD 2.7) points in intervention and 0.9 (SD 2.9) points in control (adjusted between-group difference: 0.6 points, 95%CI 0.2, 1.0; p = 0.001). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Among participants with OSA and obesity, a self-directed lifestyle intervention did not improve weight loss and led to improvements in sleep-related quality of life that are of limited clinical importance. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05104450, registered 10/19/2021.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is the accepted first-line treatment for insomnia, but its scalability and safety in patients with co-morbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (COMISA) remain unclear. Clinician-guided digital CBT-I (D-CBT-I) is a potential treatment option that may address these limitations in COMISA. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of clinician-guided D-CBT-I versus sleep hygiene education (SHE) in patients with COMISA. METHODS: This randomized trial (n = 88) compared clinician-guided D-CBT-I (6 weekly online sessions: sleep restriction, sleep hygiene, stimulus control, cognitive restructuring, relapse prevention) with SHE alone. Blinded outcome assessments were conducted at baseline, posttreatment (6 weeks), and 3-month follow-up. Primary outcomes were Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores at posttreatment and 3-month follow-up. Secondary outcomes included daytime sleepiness, sleep parameters, OSA severity, neurocognitive function, and adverse events. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: At 3-month follow-up, intention-to-treat analysis showed significantly greater improvements with D-CBT-I versus SHE on ISI (-9.5 vs. -4.0 points; d = -1.18, P = 0.001) and PSQI (-4.9 vs. -1.8 points; d = -0.87, P = 0.001); D-CBT-I also reduced subjective sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale; -3.4 vs. -1.0 points; d = -0.68, P < 0.001). At posttreatment, D-CBT-I reduced the apnea-hypopnea index (attended in-laboratory polysomnography; -6.0 vs. +2.0 events/h; d = -0.64, P = 0.019). Although transient increases in ESS occurred at weeks 2-4, no functional impairment or sleepiness-related adverse events were reported. Additional benefits were observed in metacognition and executive function. CONCLUSION: Clinician-guided D-CBT-I improved insomnia and OSA severity, and enhanced cognitive function in COMISA patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry; NO.: ChiCTR2500099854; URL: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=267457.

papers.abstract_en: The clinical adoption of deep learning in pathology is largely hindered by the "black box" nature of current models, which often obscure the biological basis of prognosis. Here, we introduce MorphX, an interpretable framework that predicts patient survival by explicitly decoding multi-scale morphological patterns from whole-slide images. Unlike conventional methods relying on latent features, MorphX fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics to attribute risk to interpretable biological phenotypes. In a multi-center study spanning 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), MorphX achieves concordance indices of 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts. Crucially, we derive eight distinct morphology-based biomarkers-driven by texture heterogeneity in necrotic regions, lymphocyte density, and nuclear shape-that demonstrate reproducible survival associations across independent cohorts, offering a granular resolution of tumor aggressiveness that transcends traditional histological grading. By translating opaque computational predictions into validated biological insights, MorphX supports trustworthy, transparent, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven precision oncology.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. METHODS: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment. FINDINGS: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group. INTERPRETATION: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended. FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover (AB/BA) trial in six adult medical ICUs of a single tertiary-care academic hospital in Bhubaneswar, India. ICUs were randomized as three ICUs of two Period of 9 months with the multicomponent oral-care bundle without chlorhexidine and three with the same bundle plus 0.12% chlorhexidine with a 1-month wash-in and re-training interval. Consecutive adults ventilated for ≥ 48 h were included. The primary outcome was VAP incidence density (Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) > 6) as per 1,000 ventilator-days. Secondary outcomes were 28-day all-cause mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, 28- day ventilator-free days, Beck Oral Assessment Scale (BOAS) and Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT) scores. The primary model was a population-averaged Poisson generalized estimating equation (GEE) and adjustment for treatment, period, sequence, age, sex, APACHE II, and SOFA. RESULTS: A total of 1,035 patients (637 No CHX, 398 CHX) accrued 10,024 ventilator-days (5,918 vs. 4,106). Groups were well balanced at baseline (mean age ≈ 55 years; APACHE II ≈ 19.6; SOFA ≈ 13.4). VAP occurred in 100/5,918 ventilator-days (16.9 per 1,000) vs. 77/4,106 (18.8 per 1,000) (No CHX vs. CHX). The adjusted Poisson incidence rate ratio was 1.08 (95% CI 0.84-1.38; p = 0.56). 28-day mortality was 28.7% vs. 26.4% (no CHX vs. CHX) (adjusted OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65-1.15; p = 0.33). ICU length of stay was longer in the CHX arm (adjusted mean difference + 0.89 days, 95% CI + 0.19 to + 1.58; p = 0.013). BOAS and CPOT scores did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, adding 0.12% chlorhexidine to a standardized oral-care bundle did not reduce VAP incidence density or 28-day mortality and was associated with a modest increase in ICU length of stay. Routine CHX use provided no clear incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU population. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Regisrty- India (CTRI) identifier [CTRI/2024/02/062201], registered [01 February 2024].

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Small-for-gestational age birth and infant linear growth faltering are prevalent in South Asia. The World Health Organization recommends balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplementation in pregnancy for undernourished populations, but evidence on the extension of supplementation through lactation to improve infant growth remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine the effect of daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on infant mean length-for-age z-score (LAZ) and secondary growth outcomes at 6 months of age. METHODS: MINT (Maternal Infant Nutrition Trial) was a 2x2 factorial, household randomized, unblinded efficacy trial to assess a daily fortified BEP supplement during pregnancy and/or lactation compared to no supplement on birth and infant growth outcomes in Sarlahi, Nepal. A modified intention-to-treat analysis estimated the effects of supplementation on infant growth outcomes using linear and Poisson regression models. Models without and with adjustment for birth size were used to estimate the overall effect and the effect independent of birth size, respectively. RESULTS: Among 1,554 mothers and 1,568 infants randomized after delivery, there was no interaction between pregnancy and lactation supplementation on the primary infant growth outcome. Neither BEP supplementation during pregnancy nor lactation had an effect on mean infant LAZ at 6 months (unadjusted mean difference for pregnancy: 0.01 [95% CI: -0.10, 0.12]; for lactation -0.02 [95% CI: -0.13, 0.09]). Significant differences were not observed for any secondary outcomes: mean weight-for-length z-scores, weight-for-age z-scores, infant weight, length, head circumference, mid-upper arm circumference or prevalence of stunting, wasting, and underweight at 6-months or for a subset of infants at 12-months. Null effects persisted after adjustment for birth size. CONCLUSIONS: In rural Nepal, daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy or early lactation did not improve linear or ponderal growth of infants at 6- or 12-months. To reduce the burden of early infant growth faltering, alternative strategies should be considered. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT03668977. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03668977?term=nct03668977&rank=1.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period. METHODS: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103. FINDINGS: Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE. INTERPRETATION: Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile. FUNDING: GSK.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. METHODS: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). FINDINGS: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156). INTERPRETATION: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. METHODS: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement. FINDINGS: Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH. INTERPRETATION: Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design. FUNDING: Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking.

papers.abstract_en: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve outcomes across several cardiometabolic conditions, but their role in World Health Organization group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective, single-center cohort study of adults with group 1 PAH. Patients prescribed SGLT2i were compared with patients without exposure. Propensity-score matching was performed 1:2 using age, sex, baseline REVEAL Lite 2 risk category, diabetes mellitus, and statin use. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events. Associations were evaluated using fixed-exposure and start-stop time-varying Cox models. The matched cohort included 366 patients: 122 (33%) receiving SGLT2i and 244 (67%) controls. Most patients were classified as high risk by REVEAL Lite 2 (106 SGLT2i recipients (87%) and 215 controls (88%), respectively). In the fixed-exposure analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53; 95% CI, 0.31-0.91; P=.018), without a significant difference in major adverse cardiovascular events (HR, 1.23; 95% CI, 0.93-1.63; P=.14). In the time-varying analysis, SGLT2i exposure was not significantly associated with mortality (HR, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.26-2.11; P=.57). The apparent survival association was attenuated after accounting for treatment timing, demonstrating the sensitivity of observational PAH estimates to exposure classification and supporting prospective randomized trials.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Phototherapies play an important role in the treatment of hyperpigmentation. However, the effects of different phototherapies on skin pigmentation have not been comprehensively evaluated to date. We analyzed the efficacy and patient satisfaction of 14 distinct phototherapies for melasma using a network meta-analysis of 22 randomized controlled trials. Cluster analysis revealed that fractional CO2 laser combines the advantages of high efficacy and patient satisfaction. We therefore evaluated the effect of fractional CO2 laser on forearm skin pigmentation in volunteers. Reflectance confocal microscopy showed that fractional CO2 laser effectively inhibited pigmentation, and the inhibitory effect was more pronounced as the scanning spacing decreased. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis revealed that fractional CO2 laser inhibited melanogenesis in photoaging skin. Transcriptome sequencing of skin samples from guinea pigs treated with fractional CO2 laser showed that the key regulators of melanogenesis (microphthalmia-associated transcription factor, tyrosinase and dopachrome tautomerase) were significantly downregulated on the seventh day after treatment with fractional CO2 laser. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis further revealed that the cyclic adenosine monophosphate signaling pathway was inhibited on the third day after treatment, whereas the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B pathway was activated on the fifth and seventh days. Fractional CO2 laser effectively reversed hyperpigmentation and may even inhibit skin pigmentation by exfoliating the superficial stratum corneum, destroying melanin granules, and regulating signaling pathways related to melanogenesis. papers.abstract_en: KRASG12D is a predominant driver in pancreatic cancer, yet the basis of intrinsic resistance to KRASG12D-targeted therapy remains poorly defined. Integrated genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics profiling across 242 patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and matched tumor tissues reveals a KRASG12D-mutant subset intrinsically resistant to KRASG12D-targeted therapeutics, characterized by marked downregulation of innate immune signaling pathways. Functional validation demonstrates that suppressing interferon signaling in sensitive models induces resistance, whereas activation of interferon signaling, particularly interferon beta (IFN-β), increases sensitivity in resistant models. Combining IFN-β with KRAS inhibitors (MRTX1133, HRS-4642, and RMC-6236) exhibits synergistic antitumor effects in intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, sustained MYC activity is associated with attenuated sensitivity to KRAS inhibition and correlates with repressed interferon signaling, suggesting a potential role in promoting intrinsic resistance. These findings identify interferon signaling as a candidate determinant of KRAS-targeted therapy response and support interferon-based combinations as a potential strategy for intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (LCCA) is an increasingly recognised yet under-characterised presentation of non-small cell lung cancer, accounting for approximately 1-4% of cases. Despite growing awareness driven by thin-section computed tomography and lung cancer screening, LCCA remains absent from major international guidelines and classifications, including those of the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer, and the World Health Organization. This narrative review synthesises the available evidence to define LCCA as a distinct clinico-radiological entity and to inform future guideline development. LCCA presents heterogeneously, with thin- or thick walled cysts, unilocular or multiloculated morphology, and variable solid components, frequently mimicking benign cysts, bullae, or emphysema. Such ambiguity contributes to diagnostic delay; in the NELSON screening trial, LCCA accounted for 22.7% of missed or delayed diagnoses. Several radiological classifications, notably that of Mascalchi, aid description and risk stratification. Conventional staging is problematic, as measurement of the solid component alone may underestimate true tumour extent, while fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography carries a high false-negative rate. Tissue sampling is similarly complicated by low diagnostic yield and false negative results, underscoring the importance of multidisciplinary team discussion. The natural history follows a stepwise progression from thin-walled cyst to wall thickening, mural nodularity, and invasive disease, with prognosis determined principally by stage, although mural nodularity and increasing solid components confer higher recurrence risk. Treatment broadly mirrors that of solid lung tumours; current guidance advocates targeting the whole cystic lesion for radical therapy rather than the solid component alone, with systemic anticancer therapy appropriate in advanced or multifocal disease. Much current practice is extrapolated from part-solid tumours; consensus on Powered by Editorial Manager® and ProduXion Manager® from Aries Systems Corporation terminology, classification, and staging, supported by prospective registry data, is required to optimise outcomes.

papers.reason: 为肺部感染快速病原学诊断提供了一种免扩增的BALF直接检测技术路线与初步分析性能基线；对胸科围手术期肺炎/术后感染的快速分层有潜在间接价值，但不改变当前胸部肿瘤诊疗决策，可作为同类BALF病原诊断研究的对照参考。
papers.abstract_en: Rapid pathogen identification is critical for timely antibiotic therapy in patients with pneumonia, yet current methods remain too slow or complex for routine clinical use. Here, we describe a localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR)-based biosensor platform that detects Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria directly in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) without nucleic acid extraction or amplification. Gold nano-islands (AuNIs) functionalized with antibodies against lipoteichoic acid (LTA) or lipopolysaccharide (LPS) enabled selective bacterial capture. The sensor achieved a refractive index resolution of 8.52 × 10-8 RIU with good reusability and dynamic range. Detection limits reached the concentration of 0.027 μM for purified LTA and 0.208 endotoxin units (EU) for LPS. When tested with Escherichia coli in artificial samples, the LPS sensor showed a reproducibility standard deviation (RSD) of 3.14%, detecting bacterial growth significantly earlier than conventional OD600 measurement. In 33 clinical BALF samples, sensor results correlated strongly with standard diagnostics (Pearson r = 0.963) and distinguished infected from noninfected cases using cutoff values of 0.060 rad (Gram-positive) and 0.083 rad (Gram-negative). The platform detects polymyxin B susceptibility 8 h earlier than conventional OD600 measurements, and a proof-of-concept sandwich immunoassay enables species-level discrimination between E. coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae. With excellent reproducibility (RSD = 3.14%), reusability over six cycles (84.21% ± 2.03% signal retention), and four-week storage stability (98.63% ± 5.42%), this LSPR platform offers a practical, rapid approach for frontline bacterial screening and accelerated antibiotic stewardship in pneumonia.

papers.abstract_en: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

papers.abstract_en: Males have lower life expectancies and greater disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) than females, and particularly poor outcomes are seen among males in marginalised contexts. In this paper, we provide an epidemiological overview and highlight the intersectional nature of men's health. We analyse mortality and DALYs data from the 1990-2023 Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Studies to illustrate our intersectional framework and draw attention to how health varies in men and to show key themes. Conditions that contribute most to the poor health of males include non-communicable diseases (eg, cardiovascular diseases and cancers), substance use, suicide, injuries (eg, road traffic incidents and interpersonal violence), and respiratory infections (eg, tuberculosis and COVID-19). Although cardiovascular disease and cancer make the largest contributions to men's higher mortality rates, determinants of health such as violence and war, migration, economic stagnation, and labour market changes due to automation and new technologies will disproportionally affect their health in the future. Injuries, violence, and other external morbidity causes often occur at a young age and in unequal distributions across the sexes, making a large contribution to DALYs. Although biology plays a role, the pattern of many diseases contributing to health differences reflects the intersection of health behaviours, shaped by patriarchy, ideas of masculinity, and structural drivers (including commercial determinants of health); many of these are preventable. Although improvements in some health behaviours are seen, exceptions occur in marginalising social conditions (eg, incarcerated men, men experiencing homelessness, men with mental illnesses, men with substance use disorders, men with low income, men who have sex with men, and those who are gender non-conforming). Multiple data sources detail men's shorter life expectancies and the drivers compared with women, but going beyond sex disaggregation remains challenging and is an urgent priority for research and health monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The 2024 McDonald criteria broaden the definition of multiple sclerosis (MS), enabling diagnosis in individuals with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria. We assessed whether these criteria identify such cases using independent laboratory/imaging biomarkers and whether these biomarkers predict subsequent disease activity. METHODS: Participants with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria were included and stratified according to the 2024 criteria. Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) and 3T brain MRI measures-including normalised brain volumes, T2 lesion load (T2LL), cortical lesion (CL) and paramagnetic rim lesion (PRL)-were compared between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2024-negative groups, and with age/sex matched McDonald2017-positive cases according to the 2017 criteria; predictors of disease activity were assessed using penalised-Cox regression. FINDINGS: A total of 141 participants were included: 95 not meeting the 2017 criteria (n = 64 asymptomatic MRI findings; n = 31 clinical presentations), stratified as McDonald2024-positive (n = 46) or McDonald2024-negative (n = 49), and 46 McDonald2017-positive cases. McDonald2024-positive vs. McDonald2024-negative cases showed higher age-corrected sNfL Z-scores (median 0.28[IQR 0.76] vs. -0.12[0.82], p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), reduced normalised thalamic volume (mean 0.009±[SD]0.0007 vs. 0.010 ± 0.0007, p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), and higher CL (1[4] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR < 0.001) and PRL (1[1] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR = 0.003) counts (differences remaining significant after age/sex, disease duration and T2LL adjustments). Biomarker profiles were comparable between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2017-positive cases. Penalised-Cox regression (n = 52) identified sNfL Z-score and PRL presence as the most consistently selected predictors of disease activity, with higher bootstrap stability for sNfL (0.84) than PRL (0.76), and good model discrimination (C-index = 0.71). INTERPRETATION: The 2024 McDonald criteria identify individuals not meeting the 2017 criteria who already exhibit MS-like neuroinflammatory/neurodegenerative pathological changes. These are reflected by laboratory and imaging biomarkers, including sNfL, which may predict subsequent disease activity and complement current diagnostic frameworks to support early clinical decision-making. FUNDING: King Baudouin Foundation; Cliniques Universitaires Saint-Luc; Fondation Charcot Stichting; Fund for Scientific Research (FNRS); ECTRIMS; Biogen; Sanofi.

papers.abstract_en: Programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunohistochemistry, the current standard biomarker for predicting response to programmed death protein 1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors in non-small cell lung cancer, has moderate predictive value among others because of tumor heterogeneity and limited biopsy representation, whereas PD-L1 PET/CT using 18F-BMS-986192 enables noninvasive, whole-tumor assessment of PD-L1 expression and heterogeneity, potentially improving prediction of response to immunotherapy. Methods: In this prospective multicenter biomarker exploration study, patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer eligible for nivolumab-based therapies underwent baseline 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT, 18F-FDG PET/CT, and tumor biopsy for PD-L1 immunohistochemistry before treatment initiation. The primary endpoint was durable clinical benefit, defined as progression-free survival (PFS) of 9 mo or greater, with secondary analyses assessing associations among tracer uptake, PD-L1 expression, survival outcomes, and PET-based radiomic features. Results: Of 91 enrolled patients, 77 were included in the final analysis of 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT. Although PD-L1 immunohistochemistry did not differ between patients with PFS of less than 9 mo versus 9 mo or greater, PD-L1 PET uptake in lung lesions was significantly higher in patients with PFS of at least 9 mo (P = 0.01). Using an optimal mean SUVpeak cutoff of 2.4, PD-L1 PET demonstrated a high negative predictive value (94%) for durable clinical benefit, with significant associations for both PFS and overall survival, particularly in patients receiving first-line treatment. Tracer uptake showed no correlation with 18F-FDG uptake. Conclusion: 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT revealed interpatient PD-L1 variability. Low uptake in lung lesions predicted poor outcomes with high negative predictive value. 18F-BMS-986192 PET/CT demonstrated stronger negative predictive value than did baseline PD-L1 immunohistochemistry in this cohort. These findings require prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The triglyceride high-density lipoprotein cholesterol-glucose body mass index (TyHGB) is a novel composite indicator integrating triglyceride, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, fasting glucose and body mass index and may provide a more comprehensive assessment of systemic metabolic status than current indices. This multicenter landmark cohort study aimed to determine the association between TyHGB measured at the landmark time and 28-day mortality in patients present in the intensive care units (ICUs) at that time and to evaluate its potential utility as a prognostic marker. METHODS: This multicenter observational cohort study included 1649 patients from 113 ICUs in China. The association between TyHGB and 28-day mortality was evaluated using three sequentially adjusted logistic regression models with restricted cubic splines: Model 1 adjusted for demographics; Model 2 further adjusted for disease severity and organ dysfunction; Model 3 additionally adjusted for therapeutic interventions. Subgroup analyses with interaction tests were conducted. Model performance was assessed by discrimination (AUC), calibration (Brier score and calibration slope) and internal validation via bootstrap resamples. RESULTS: Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a positive association between TyHGB and 28-day mortality across fully adjusted models (P < 0.05). Subgroup analyses identified a statistically significant interaction with diabetes (P for interaction = 0.011). In the overall cohort, adding TyHGB to the base model improved AUC from 0.731 to 0.745 (ΔAUC = +0.014, P = 0.043), with significant improvements in reclassification (NRI = 0.328, P < 0.001; IDI = 0.012, P = 0.009) and model fit (LRT P < 0.001). Among diabetic patients (N = 401), TyHGB significantly improved AUC from 0.673 to 0.723 (ΔAUC = +0.050, P = 0.049; NRI = 0.515, P < 0.001; IDI = 0.041, P = 0.022). In contrast, no significant improvement was observed in non-diabetic patients (ΔAUC = +0.009, P = 0.152). CONCLUSION: Among patients present in participating ICUs at the landmark time, higher TyHGB was associated with subsequent 28-day mortality. However, adding TyHGB to the baseline risk prediction model led to only small improvements in overall predictive performance. Findings in diabetic patients are exploratory and require further validation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Adherence to American Heart Association (AHA) ventilation guidelines during cardiac arrest is challenging. METHODS: Prospective, Before/After quality assurance study determining adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by Milwaukee County Emergency Medical Services and Kenosha Fire in Wisconsin using (Before) end tidal carbon dioxide [ETCO2] to monitor ventilations - Real BVM Help® applied but blinded versus (After) Real BVM Help®. PRIMARY ENDPOINTS: mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in-target for rate, tidal volume, and both rate and tidal volume. AHA 2020 guidelines were followed. RESULTS: From 9/29/22-12/22/23, 278 patients were entered (148 Before/130 After). Average age: 62.3±16.7 years; 185 (67%) male. Mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in Before/After Groups in-target for rate (47.7±25.1% vs 74.4±24.1% respectively, p<0.0001), tidal volume (15.3±15.4% vs 45.4±23.8% respectively, p<0.0001), and rate and tidal volume (7.5±9.6% vs 39.0±23.3% respectively, p<0.0001) were significantly higher in the After Group. In the Before Group, using ETCO2 to monitor all ventilations (N=22,037 ventilations), only 43.8% were in-target for rate, 13.5% in-target for tidal volume, and 6.8% in-target for rate and tidal volume with a lower-than-target tidal volume delivered in 58.2% of all ventilations. CONCLUSION: Real BVM Help® was associated with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines. ETCO2 monitoring failed to approach both rate and tidal volume guideline adherence with a lower-than-target tidal volume being the most common parameter delivered out-of-target (58.2%). Ventilation rate and tidal volume monitoring with real-time feedback should be considered during treatment of cardiac arrest.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Recurrent cardiac arrest (rearrest) after initial return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) is associated with relatively poor outcomes. Early identification of rearrest might allow for intervention to prevent rearrest. In this study, we sought to determine whether clinical ECG features can predict rearrest. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients who achieved ROSC between 2018-2024. We evaluated the association of ECG features (QRS width, standard deviation of NN intervals, root mean square of successive NN interval differences, and percentage of NN intervals that differ by more than 50 milliseconds) within individual 15-second segments throughout a 5-minute window prior to rearrest as well as their temporal trends over the 5-minute analytic window. RESULTS: Of the 1,489 OHCA patients achieving ROSC, 1,298 were analyzed; 528 (40.7%) experienced rearrest. Rearrest patients were older, less likely to receive bystander CPR (48.7% vs. 61.9%), and had lower survival (20.4% vs. 43.1%) and favorable neurologic outcomes (7.8% vs. 21.2%; all p<0.001). We found lower heart rate, wider QRS, and higher HR variability in those with rearrest. Identification was highest 1 minute prior to rearrest (AUROC 0.74), declining beyond 3 minutes. Models using temporal trends achieved AUROC 0.67; strongest predictors were heart rate variability measures and QRS width. CONCLUSION: Established ECG features achieved good prediction for rearrest with identification improving closer to time of rearrest. Future work leveraging novel features or more advanced artificial intelligence models may further improve prediction.

papers.abstract_en: Anthropomorphic design is widely assumed to shape self-disclosure and emotional dependence by first cultivating felt empathy and trust, and the safety measures platforms deploy, such as labelling and disclosure of artificial origin, target those perceptions. Across a twelve-country survey, forty-seven interviews, and three experiments, this research tests that mediation model and identifies the route that carries the behavioural effect. A twelve-country survey (N = 1480) found empathy and trust negligibly related to disclosure and dependence at the trait level. Two experiments (N = 390 and N = 300) produced strong direct effects of an anthropomorphic agent, with the anthropomorphic agent roughly tripling the odds of behavioural disclosure (63% versus 35% under a matched neutral prompt), while the indirect effects through empathy and trust received no support. Study 5 (N = 300) measured competing mediators and provided the most defensible interim account of the mechanism: only perceived anonymity and reduced evaluation apprehension carried the effect on disclosure, locating the process in online disinhibition rather than felt relational warmth. Forty-seven interviews surfaced clinically salient disclosure, including suicidal ideation revealed to a chatbot and to no person. Because the consequences of anthropomorphic design travel through the lowered social risk of the medium, safeguards that recalibrate how users perceive an agent may leave disclosure and dependence largely untouched.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Relapsed/refractory (R/R) lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a clinical challenge with limited therapies and poor prognosis. CAR‑NK cell therapy has shown promise in solid tumors, but its efficacy is limited by both the availability of effective targets and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. CD73 (NT5E), highly expressed across solid tumors, catalyzes adenosine production to drive immunosuppression, representing both a specific CAR‑NK target and a key leverage point to overcome tumor immune evasion. However, its systematic evaluation as a therapeutically actionable target for CAR‑NK cell therapy in R/R LUAD remains unexplored. METHODS: We first characterized CD73 expression through integrative analysis of public datasets, primary and relapsed clinical LUAD specimens, and LUAD cell lines derived from primary and metastatic tumors. We then constructed CD73‑CAR‑NK cells and assessed their in vitro cytotoxicity across LUAD cell lines of varying malignancy, as well as their effects on extracellular adenosine and resistance to adenosine‑mediated immunosuppression. Finally, we assessed their antitumor efficacy in a stepwise manner across a tiered panel of in vivo models, including cell line‑derived xenograft (CDX), metastasis, patient‑derived xenograft (PDX), and clinically relevant immune‑humanized PDX models. RESULTS: CD73 expression was elevated in metastasis-derived LUAD cell lines and R/R LUAD specimens. Accordingly, CD73-CAR-NK92 cells exhibited potent cytotoxicity against CD73-high LUAD cells, accompanied by an activated effector phenotype, reduced extracellular adenosine, partial resistance to adenosine-mediated suppression, and limited activity toward normal bronchial epithelial cells. Notably, this enhanced function was consistently observed across multiple NK cell sources including peripheral blood-derived NK (PBNK), umbilical cord blood‑derived NK (UBNK), and iPSC-derived NK (iNK). In vivo, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, with enhanced tumor‑site enrichment, prolonged retention, and elevated intratumoral levels of TNF‑α and IFN‑γ. Importantly, in an immune‑humanized PDX mouse model, CD73‑CAR‑NK92 cells significantly reduced the growth of R/R patient‑derived xenografts, accompanied by immune remodeling, without marked systemic inflammation during the observation period. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide preclinical evidence that CD73-CAR-NK cells exhibit potent antitumor efficacy for R/R LUAD through their dual functions of eliminating CD73-high tumor cells and resisting adenosine-mediated immunosuppressive signaling, supporting their therapeutic potential.

papers.abstract_en: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

papers.abstract_en: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8+ T cell activity, whereas CD8+ T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8+ T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

papers.abstract_en: Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a subtype of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) and a rare, life-threatening complication of uncontrolled rheumatic diseases, characterized by systemic inflammation driven by aberrant activation of macrophages. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of plonmarlimab, a high-affinity neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), for the treatment of MAS. In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm clinical trial (NCT07034209 and CTR20230579), 18 patients with MAS secondary to systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease who were refractory to or had relapsed after high-dose glucocorticoid therapy were enrolled. Patients received plonmarlimab once weekly for 8 weeks at 6 mg/kg as the starting in the accelerated titration stage, and then at 10 mg/kg for the first two doses followed by dose adjustments at the investigator's discretion. The primary endpoint, overall response rate at week 8, was 83.3% (15/18) among all treated patients. The median time to response was 2.1 weeks (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.0-3.1), and the median time to remission of MAS symptoms was 1.1 weeks (95% CI, 1.0-2.3). The least-squares mean percentage reduction in glucocorticoid dose from baseline to week 8 was 79.3% (95% CI, 76.3-82.3), and 83.3% of patients (15/18) achieved a ≥ 50% reduction. No grade ≥ 3 infections were observed. Biomarker analysis showed rapid reductions in ferritin and interleukin (IL)-18 levels. Plonmarlimab showed promising clinical activity and was generally well tolerated in patients with MAS, and IL-18 may serve as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for GM-CSF antibody therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide and disproportionately affects older adults. As population ageing accelerates, the global cancer burden among older adults continues to increase. This study systematically evaluated the latest global cancer burden and its epidemiological characteristics among older adults. METHODS: Data on the incidence and mortality of 33 malignancies, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, among adults aged 65 + were extracted from the Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024 and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 databases and stratified by age, sex, region, and Human Development Index (HDI). Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) were calculated. Annual percentage changes (APC) were used to characterize temporal trends. Decomposition analysis was performed to quantify the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological changes. Demographic projection methods and generalized additive model (GAM) were applied to forecast the cancer burden through 2050. RESULTS: In 2024, there were 9,966,392 new cancer cases and 6,001,290 cancer deaths among older adults worldwide, accounting for 51.11% and 61.84%, respectively, of all-age totals. Lung, colorectal, stomach, liver, and prostate cancers were leading causes of death. Incidence and mortality were higher in men and increased with age. The Western Pacific Region had the largest burden, whereas Europe Region had the highest ASIR. ASIR correlated positively with HDI (rs = 0.771), while mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) correlated negatively (rs = -0.825). From 2000 to 2023, ASIR and ASMR declined, although burden increased, primarily driven by population growth; pancreatic cancer exhibited the most rapid increase. Tobacco use remained the leading risk factor for mortality, while metabolic risks rose in importance. Under a demographic scenario assuming constant 2024 age-specific rates and changes only in population size and age structure, new cancer cases and deaths among older adults are projected to reach approximately 19.8 million and 12.5 million by 2050, roughly double the 2024 figures, with the largest increase in the Eastern Mediterranean region. CONCLUSION: Cancer burden in older adults is substantial, varying by sex, age, region, and development level. Precision prevention and control are urgently needed, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. REGISTRY AND THE REGISTRATION NO. OF THE STUDY/TRIAL: N/A.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intraluminal obstruction produces chronic airway epithelial hypoxia. We investigated how chronic airway epithelial hypoxia and inflammatory stimuli interact in human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cultures and resected human bronchiectatic lungs to produce an airway epithelial environment characteristic of muco-obstructive disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HBE cultures were exposed to normoxia or hypoxia (1% O2) for 5 days, followed by administration of supernatants from cystic fibrosis (CF) lung-derived mucopurulent material (SMM) or PBS for 24 h. A reverse order protocol with SMM followed by hypoxia was also performed. Bulk RNA-sequencing and functional (Na+ transport) studies were performed. HIF1A and EPAS1-mediated transcriptional responses were characterised in CRISPR knockdown HBE cells. RNA in situ hybridisation studies of excised bronchiectatic lungs and bioinformatic analyses of published datasets tested for relevance of in vitro findings to in vivo conditions. RESULTS: Hypoxia and SMM regulated largely separate airway epithelial transcriptional programmes regardless of treatment order. PTGS2 (COX-2), CCL20, MUC5B, and CXCL8 (IL-8) represented a small number of genes upregulated by both hypoxia and SMM. HIF1A knockdown and EPAS1 knockdown produced distinct, often opposing, effects on hypoxia-responsive pathways. HIF1A dominated upregulation of glycolytic pathway signalling. EPAS1 regulated genes that increase mucus concentration under hypoxia (e.g., SCNN1G). An EPAS1 inhibitor blocked hypoxia-induced upregulation of Na+ transport. CONCLUSION: Chronic hypoxia and inflammation regulated distinct genes/pathways that combine to produce a complex diseased environment in muco-obstructed airway epithelia. HIF1A and EPAS1 regulated distinct hypoxia-induced transcriptional responses. EPAS1 inhibition may exhibit a favourable therapeutic ratio for treatment of muco-obstructive lung diseases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Short-term peripheral nerve stimulation serves as a neuromodulation therapy that modulates neural activity to provide therapeutic benefit, particularly pain relief. This study investigated the effectiveness of short-term peripheral nerve stimulation as a minimally invasive approach for achieving pain relief. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from database inception till September 10, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults comparing short-term peripheral nerve stimulation with sham stimulation or usual care. The primary outcome was the change in average pain intensity during the implantation period. RESULTS: Eight RCTs (543 participants) were included. Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed significant reductions in average pain intensity during the implantation period at 1-4 weeks (SMD = -0.48, 95% CI = -0.71 to -0.26, P < 0.0001) and 5-8 weeks (SMD = -0.96, 95% CI = -1.22 to -0.70, P < 0.0001), but no significant result after electrode removal. For worst pain intensity, the intervention group showed a greater reduction than the control group at all time periods except 1-4 weeks after EOT. Improvements in pain interference were delayed, becoming significant at 5-8 weeks during the implantation period (MD = -1.34, 95% CI = -1.86 to -0.82, P < 0.00001) and ≥8 weeks after the end of treatment (MD = -1.09, 95%CI = -1.69 to -0.50, P = 0.0003). Subgroup analyses showed improvements in postoperative pain. The usual care-controlled subgroup showed more pronounced and sustained benefits than the sham-controlled subgroup, and the chronic pain subgroup also showed more pronounced and sustained benefits compared to the acute/subacute pain subgroup. CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis provided preliminary evidence that short-term peripheral nerve stimulation may relieve pain during the implantation period, but not all outcomes suggest sustained improvements after electrode removal. REGISTRATION PROSPERO: CRD420251243978.

papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin resistance is a major obstacle in the treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). To address this challenge, we screened a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug library and identified fingolimod, an immunomodulatory agent, as a potent inhibitor of cisplatin-resistant ESCC cells. Fingolimod is likely to directly binds to Glu266 of the nuclear pore complex protein NUP54, promoting its proteasomal degradation. This disrupts the NUP54-NUP58-NUP62 central channel, impairing the nuclear import of the key DNA repair protein SPIDR. Consequently, fingolimod treatment inhibits the recruitment of the SPIDR-RAD51-DMC1 complex by chromatin, causing defective homologous recombination repair, accumulation of DNA damage, and ultimately, the reversal of cisplatin resistance. In addition, fingolimod restored the sensitivity of cisplatin to ESCC treatment in both patient-derived xenograft and organoid models. Our study unveils a novel mechanism by which fingolimod targets the nuclear pore complex to suppress DNA repair, providing a compelling rationale for repurposing fingolimod as a combination therapy to overcome cisplatin resistance in ESCC.

papers.results: 分析验证：inclusivity 97%、exclusivity 96%、精密度CV<15%，四个数量级内线性定量。临床验证：BALF-mcfDNA在34%的受试者中检出可能的肺炎病原，常规检测为24%，诊断产出提高43%（与常规检测合并时为57%）；在24%的一致病例中，mcfDNA测序通过识别新病原或种级病原提供了额外的临床相关信息。

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Rapid and comprehensive detection of respiratory pathogens is essential for immunocompromised patients with suspected pneumonia. Conventional diagnostic methods are limited in scope, often slow, and lack sensitivity, leading to reduced diagnostic yield. OBJECTIVES: To analytically and clinically validate a microbial cell-free DNA (mcfDNA) sequencing assay for bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) that enables broad and sensitive detection of pathogens causing pneumonia in immunocompromised patients. METHODS: The BALF-mcfDNA assay detects more than 500 bacteria, DNA viruses, fungi, and parasites. Analytical validation used 324 contrived samples containing DNA from 11 representative organisms and 1,294 in-silico samples. Clinical validation compared BALF-mcfDNA sequencing with usual care (UC) testing in 118 immunocompromised adults with suspected pneumonia. An independent expert panel adjudicated the etiologic diagnoses. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: BALF-mcfDNA testing demonstrated high inclusivity (97%), exclusivity (96%), and precision (coefficient of variation < 15%), with linear quantification across four orders of magnitude. Limits of detection were consistent across taxa, GC content, and genome size. In clinical evaluation, BALF-mcfDNA sequencing identified probable pneumonia pathogens in 34% of participants versus 24% for UC testing, increasing diagnostic yield by 43% (57% when combined with UC). In 24% of concordant cases, mcfDNA sequencing provided additional clinically relevant information by identifying new or species-level pathogens. CONCLUSIONS: BALF-mcfDNA sequencing enables sensitive, comprehensive, and rapid pathogen detection from BALF specimens, outperforming conventional methods and improving etiologic diagnosis of pneumonia in immunocompromised hosts.

papers.abstract_en: Capillary leak syndrome (CLS) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition characterized by generalized edema, hypotension, and hypoalbuminemia. Amivantamab has recently been approved for the management of metastatic NSCLC. Although peripheral edema has been reported with amivantamab, CLS has not previously been described in association with this treatment. Herein, we report a case of CLS attributed to amivantamab that resolved after drug discontinuation and a short course of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin administration. The anti-inflammatory, neutralizing, and antibody clearance-accelerating effects of intravenous immunoglobulin may explain their potential efficacy in treating amivantamab-induced CLS. As therapeutic antibodies become increasingly used, CLS may be encountered more frequently. A better understanding of its pathophysiologic characteristics is therefore essential to develop effective treatments and preventive strategies, ultimately minimizing its consequences on patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the predominant subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, is characterized by high incidence, poor prognosis, limited therapeutic efficacy. Glycolysis-high LUAD is associated with aggressive tumor behavior and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that broadly impairs anti-tumor immunity and therapeutic efficacy. Effective strategies targeting this metabolically aggressive phenotype are urgently needed. In this study, we developed a combination strategy that modulates DEPDC1-associated glycolysis by integrating fluvastatin (Fluv) with an integrin αVβ3-targeted photodynamic nanoplatform (cRGD-TPA-DCR-NP, with light irradiation; NPL), termed Fluv + NPL. Integrated multi-omics analyses, together with Western blotting and glycolytic rate (GlycoPER) measurements, demonstrated that Fluv + NPL suppressed DEPDC1-mediated NF-κB signaling, thereby inhibiting PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway activity and reducing glycolytic metabolism in LUAD cells. Simultaneously, Fluv + NPL downregulated exosomal CCL2 levels and inhibited M2 macrophage polarization. In vivo studies further showed that Fluv + NPL effectively modulated the immune microenvironment of LUAD, as evidenced by enhanced M1 macrophage polarization, increased infiltration of effector T cells, and reduced M2 macrophage abundance, ultimately resulting in significant inhibition of LUAD growth. Collectively, our findings reveal an important role of DEPDC1 in linking glycolytic metabolism to immune regulation and establish Fluv + NPL as a promising therapeutic strategy that simultaneously suppresses glycolysis and enhances antitumor immunity through modulation of DEPDC1. These results provide new insights into glycolytic metabolism-immunity-based combination therapies for LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) promotes tuberculosis pathogenesis in part by exploiting host pyroptosis, yet bacterial factors that directly engage the pyroptotic executioner machinery remain poorly defined. Here we identify the ESX-5 component EccB5 as a mycobacterial virulence factor that binds gasdermin D (GSDMD) and potentiates pathogenic pyroptosis. A proteome-wide screen using GSDMD as bait revealed EccB5 as a specific interactor, mapped to the EccB5 C terminus and residue R406. Purified protein assays demonstrated micromolar affinity direct binding between EccB5 and GSDMD, with a dissociation constant of 5.22 μM by surface plasmon resonance. In vivo, conditional ATc-inducible knockdown of eccB5 in the Mtb H37Rv strain markedly reduces lung pathology, bacterial burden, and host cell death in mice. Conversely, ectopic expression of EccB5 in nonpathogenic Mycobacterium smegmatis is sufficient to trigger robust macrophage pyroptosis and amplify inflammatory responses in mice. Mechanistically, EccB5 enhances canonical inflammasome-associated GSDMD processing and promotes NLRP3-dependent GSDMD-N membrane association and oligomerization, without evidence of caspase-3/GSDME activation or noncanonical inflammasome engagement. Genetic ablation of host GSDMD abolishes EccB5-driven pyroptotic responses, establishing GSDMD as an essential host target. Together, these findings define an ESX5-linked virulence axis that directly couples mycobacterial infection to the execution phase of pyroptosis, thereby facilitating Mtb dissemination and disease progression. Targeting the EccB5-GSDMD interface provides a mechanistically grounded strategy for host-directed therapy in tuberculosis.

papers.abstract_en: X-linked myotubular myopathy (XLMTM) is caused by mutations in the MTM1 gene that encodes the myotubularin protein, essential for normal muscle development and function. XLMTM manifests as profound muscle weakness and hypotonia at birth, leading to severe respiratory insufficiency, and in many cases, early death. Resamirigene bilparvovec (rAAV8-Des-hMTM1) is a muscle-directed, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapy in clinical development for the treatment of XLMTM. In the first-in-human clinical trial (ASPIRO; NCT03199469), rAAV8-Des-hMTM1 was associated with reduced ventilator dependence and unprecedented improvements in motor function in boys with XLMTM. However, four of the 24 participants who received rAAV8-Des-hMTM1 died after developing cholestatic liver failure. Safety results from large-animal studies of rAAV8-Des-MTM1 are presented herein and discussed retrospectively in the context of the adverse events observed in the clinical trial. Healthy infant cynomolgus monkeys and juvenile XLMTM dogs received relatively high doses of rAAV8-Des-hMTM1, or its canine version (rAAV8-Des-cMTM1), respectively. In both species, vector genomes were highest in liver, while myotubularin expression was highest in cardiac or skeletal muscle. rAAV8-Des-MTM1 was generally well-tolerated; importantly, there was no evidence of hyperbilirubinemia or other liver-associated toxicity following rAAV8-Des-MTM1 administration to cynomolgus monkeys or XLMTM dogs.

papers.abstract_en: Dravet Syndrome (DS) is a catastrophic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) primarily caused by SCN1A haploinsufficiency. It is characterized by refractory hyperthermia-induced seizures, neurodevelopmental delay, and an elevated risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) compared to other childhood epilepsies. While the small molecule fenfluramine (FFA) provides profound clinical benefit, its potential for systemic side effects and a poorly defined mechanism of action (MOA) underscores the need for more targeted interventions. Using a Scn1a+/- rat model of DS, we demonstrate that chronic FFA treatment reduces the frequency of hyperthermia-induced seizures and attenuates pathological EEG network hypersynchrony. Furthermore, FFA administration ameliorates hyperactivity and depressive-like comorbidities, an effect associated with a marked reduction in hippocampal neuroinflammation and microglial overactivation. Transcriptomic analysis implicated serotonergic signaling in the therapeutic response to FFA, and subsequent anatomical and functional analyses revealed enhanced activity of dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic neurons following FFA treatment. Cell-type-specific AAV-mediated modulation of DRN serotonergic neurons was sufficient to reproduce the key antiseizure and electrophysiological effects of FFA. Together, our findings identify the DRN serotonergic circuit as a therapeutically relevant circuit and provide proof-of-concept for mechanism-driven, circuit-specific neuromodulation strategies for Dravet syndrome.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Yersinia pestis (Y. pestis), the bacterial pathogen responsible for plague in humans, remains a public health threat, particularly in light of the recent emergence of antibiotic resistance strains. METHODS: To better understand the immune response against plague and to identify potential targets for immunointervention, we performed an epitope mapping study of the IgG response against a library of peptides representing 18 Y. pestis proteins. The study included sera from 51 individuals who had recovered from plague, 26 uninfected human controls, and 20 sera from mice protected by a live-attenuated vaccine. FINDINGS: Analysis of human sera revealed 32 reactive peptides distributed across eight protein antigens, whereas analysis of mouse sera identified 187 reactive peptides spanning all 18 proteins. Combined analysis of the human and mouse IgG responses to the 32 human-reactive peptides identified 27 B-cell epitopes located within YopD, YopB, LcrV, FyuA, Pla, Ail, Caf1, and PsaA. Of these, one epitope had previously been described as protective and another as immunodominant, whereas the remaining 25 represent immunodominant epitopes identified in this study. INTERPRETATION: Interestingly, IgG antibody responses to selected YopD and YopB peptides were significantly stronger in pneumonic plague than in bubonic plague, suggesting that the distinct clinical manifestations of the disease may be associated with distinct underlying pathophysiological and molecular mechanisms. Our comprehensive mapping of linear IgG epitopes recognised by convalescent human sera, combined with prioritisation based on their predicted neutralising potential, provides a resource for future studies evaluating peptide-based diagnostics, vaccines, and monoclonal antibody therapies against plague. FUNDING: The project was supported by a grant from Agence Nationale de la Recherche (ANR).
