papers.abstract_en: Early diagnosis and accurate staging are essential for improving treatment efficacy and clinical outcomes of pancreatic cancer (PC), but remain challenging because of limited early PC-specific biomarkers and high-performance detection methods. In this paper, we developed a machine learning (ML)-enhanced terahertz (THz)-colorimetric dual-mode metadevice based on metallic nanonetworks for multiplexed microRNA (miRNA) detection and early PC diagnosis. Clinical sample measurements and bioinformatics analysis identified miRNA-21, miRNA-1290, and miRNA-320a as candidate PC biomarkers. Target miRNAs triggered the assembly of DNA-functionalized Fe and Au nanoparticles (NPs) with PEI-modified CuS NPs into ternary Fe/Au/Cu nanonetworks, generating THz and colorimetric signals through their dielectric and peroxidase-like properties. This target-triggered assembly enabled three-miRNA panel analysis without enzyme-mediated nucleic acid amplification and achieved attomolar-level miRNA profiling. Six ML algorithms were integrated to develop predictive models for PC diagnosis and staging. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) achieved diagnostic accuracies of 97.8% (95% CI: 88.2-99.9%) in the training cohort (n = 45) and 96.7% (95% CI: 82.8-99.9%) in the validation cohort (n = 30), with 100% sensitivity for early PC in both cohorts. Compared with CA19-9, CA125, and CEA, the multiplexed miRNA-based dual-mode metadevice showed higher efficacy (area under the curve, AUC: 1.00 vs 0.905), supporting its potential for clinical miRNA-based liquid biopsy.

papers.abstract_en: Real-time, ppm-to-ppb-level detection of hydrogen (H2) remains essential for industrial safety, given its flammability and widespread use in energy applications. Portable H2 sensors, however, continue to suffer from insufficient sensitivity and reliance on elevated operating temperatures. Here, cubic bixbyite In2O3 nanocubes, synthesized by radio frequency sputtering at 600 °C, were functionalized via drop-cast decoration with ZnS nanoparticles to form an n-n heterojunction for H2 sensing at room temperature (∼32 °C). The ZnS/In2O3 architecture leverages a high surface area, oxygen vacancy-mediated adsorption, and catalytic spillover from ZnS to enhance H2 interaction and charge carrier modulation. Pristine In2O3 showed a relative response of 11.23% to 50 ppm H2, which increased to ∼23% upon optimal ZnS loading (48 wt %), with a detection limit of 86.9 ppb and response/recovery times of ∼90 s/∼488 s. To enable quantitative concentration estimation, a two-stage machine learning framework was developed using six transient response features (Smax, Trsp (90%), Trec (90%), ∫Rdt, mean dR/dt, and ∫R/s). Permutation importance identified Trec (90%), mean dR/dt, and ∫R/s as dominant predictors, while principal component analysis captured 91.8% variance with clear concentration-dependent clustering. Among four regressors evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation, Gaussian process regression achieved the best static prediction (root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 4.044 ppm, R2 = 0.945), while a 15 s sliding-window multilayer perceptron model with Bayesian-optimized hyperparameters enabled real-time tracking (RMSE = 3.837 ppm, mean absolute error = 1.263 ppm, and R2 = 0.924) across 0.5-50 ppm, with sub-5 ppm resolution well below the 4 vol % lower flammability limits. These results establish a combined materials and data-driven strategy for robust, ambient-temperature H2 monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The updated New Zealand asthma guidelines in 2020, aligning with global asthma guideline recommendations, advocated for a fundamental shift from short-acting β2-agonist (SABA) reliever therapy to anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR) therapy (ICS-formoterol) in adults and adolescents. While aggregate population-level data indicate increased ICS-formoterol dispensings, patient-level changes in medication use remain unclear. We examined medication use patterns to assess early practice changes across the entire asthma population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study using the New Zealand national linked health datasets. Patients aged ≥12 with asthma were identified from hospitalisation and/or dispensing data, and categorised by the complete set of inhaler classes dispensed in the three months preceding their final dispensing date within the baseline (July 2018-June 2020) and post-guideline (June 2020-June 2022) periods. Nine mutually exclusive categories were defined without applying any hierarchy between medications: SABA only; ICS, non-formoterol ICS-LABA, and ICS-formoterol, each with and without a concurrently dispensed SABA; other regimens; and no inhaled medication. Age subgroups (12-44 and ≥ 45 years) were examined. Children aged < 12 years throughout follow-up, who were outside the scope of the recommendation, served as a comparison cohort for difference-in-differences estimation. FINDINGS: The cohort included 324,972 patients aged ≥12 years. At baseline, the SABA-only group was the most common (30.5%). Post-guideline, dispensing of the guideline-recommended regimen, ICS-formoterol without SABA, more than doubled from 10.9% to 23.8%, and any ICS-formoterol use rose from 18.9% to 34.5%. The proportion of patients dispensed any SABA fell from 74.1% to 60.8%. Of patients dispensed SABA only pre-guideline, 57.1% were dispensed SABA only again, while 17.6% changed to ICS-formoterol without SABA and 8.1% to ICS-formoterol with SABA. Continuity was high among patients on maintenance therapy (55.9% for ICS, 74.3% for non-formoterol ICS-LABA) and among those already dispensed ICS-formoterol (89.0%). Among post-guideline ICS-formoterol users, 31.1% were also dispensed a SABA, compared with 63.8% of non-formoterol ICS-LABA users and 70.2% of ICS users. Using children aged < 12 years as a comparison cohort, difference-in-differences estimates were +8.4 percentage points for ICS-formoterol without SABA and -8.3 percentage points for total SABA supply, but -0.2 percentage points for SABA monotherapy. INTERPRETATION: The impact of the guideline change was substantial but selective. While the update facilitated transition for patients already receiving maintenance therapy, most patients on SABA-only regimens did not switch to the preferred AIR regimen. Further targeted implementation strategies beyond guideline publication are required to address this gap and ensure evidence-based care is consistently delivered. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perennial leguminous shrubs of the genus Caragana play key roles in arid and semi-arid ecosystems, contributing to ecological restoration, nitrogen fixation, and bioenergy production. However, the genomic basis underlying their adaptation to arid environments remains insufficiently understood. RESULTS: Here, we generate chromosome-scale genome assemblies for 14 representative Caragana species, including a near telomere-to-telomere assembly of Caragana korshinskii (NMCN13). Using these genomes, we construct a graph-based pan-genome and identify extensive genomic variation, including 801,351 structural variants and 104,404 presence-absence variations. Comparative analyses identify clade-specific gene family expansions enriched in stress-related pathways, particularly secondary metabolism. We further identify two candidate drought-responsive genes, CkoERF1 and CkoWAKL, whose functions are supported by heterologous overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana and alfalfa, demonstrating enhanced drought-response phenotypes. Transposable element analyses indicate that variation in LTR retrotransposon abundance contributes to genome size diversity across species. Notably, we find that some key symbiosis-related genes, for example, NIN, DMI1, DMI2, and NSP1, are conserved across all species, suggesting a stable genetic basis for nitrogen fixation. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides high-quality genomic resources and a comprehensive pan-genomic framework for Caragana. Our findings offer new insights into genome evolution, environmental adaptation, and drought tolerance mechanisms, and establish a foundation for future functional genomics and breeding efforts in leguminous shrubs.

papers.abstract_en: Centromeres are essential for chromosome segregation, yet their organization and evolution remain poorly understood in polyploid crops. We present the first complete telomere-to-telomere reference genome of Brassica napus cultivar Zhongshuang11 and characterize centromere architecture and evolution. We identify core satellite repeats that define centromeres and reveal extensive sequence polymorphism and structural divergence between subgenomes associated with polyploidization and domestication. We further uncover rDNA-enriched pericentromeres generated by recurrent chromosome rearrangements and propose a centromere evolutionary cycle model that explains how satellite repeats and transposons jointly shape centromere evolution.

papers.abstract_en: A major challenge in integrating previously analyzed single-cell RNA-seq studies is the inconsistency of cell type annotations. To address this, we developed GCTHarmony, an LLM-based method for harmonizing cell type annotations across single-cell studies. Utilizing OpenAI's text embedding model, GCTHarmony accurately maps arbitrary cell type annotations to standardized cell ontology terms and reconciles discrepancies in annotation hierarchies across studies. In real data examples, we show that GCTHarmony substantially improves the consistency of cell type annotations across single-cell studies.

papers.abstract_en: Chromatin state annotations based on epigenetic marks are powerful resources, but many additional samples have gene expression data available while lacking epigenetic mark data and chromatin state annotations. Using the EpiATLAS resource of the International Human Epigenome Consortium (IHEC), we develop Gene Expression-based Chromatin State Imputation (GECSI), which uses an ensemble of multi-class logistic regression classifiers to predict chromatin state annotations from gene expression data. We show in cross-validation that GECSI accurately predicts observed chromatin state annotations. We also apply GECSI using gene expression data in 449 IHEC additional samples, providing an expanded chromatin state annotation resource.

papers.abstract_en: The IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling axis mediates cellular communication in various contexts and has recently been implicated in pro-fibrotic responses. However, its specific role in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), which is characterized by abundant cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), remains elusive. Here, we investigated the contribution of IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling to CAF function and OSCC progression. Immunohistochemical analysis of patient samples revealed that IL-36γ was highly expressed in CAFs and that higher co-expression of IL-36γ/IL-36R in CAFs was associated with more invasive patterns and shorter disease-free survival. By integrating tumor cell lines with patient-derived organoids (PDOs), we established three co-culture systems to model these interactions. These models revealed that IL-36γ signaling enhanced CAF proliferation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Mechanistically, the IL-36γ/IL-36R axis in CAFs increased ERK1/2-dependent CCL20 secretion, which in turn promoted tumor cell invasion. Pharmacological blockade of IL-36R attenuated both the IL-36γ-induced increase in CAF abundance and the associated pro-tumorigenic CAF phenotypes in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that the IL-36γ/IL-36R-ERK1/2-CCL20 signaling cascade participates in CAF-tumor interactions. Targeting IL-36R may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy for invasive OSCC.

papers.abstract_en: Activated Cdc42-associated kinase 1 (ACK1; encoded by the TNK2 gene) is an oncogenic protein of the non-receptor tyrosine kinase family and functions downstream of RAS and activated transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinases such as EGFR. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which constitutes around 85% of lung cancer cases, often exhibits amplification or overexpression of the TNK2 gene. This study focuses on demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting ACK1 for the treatment of NSCLC. The small molecule ACK1 inhibitor, (R)-9b, preferentially inhibited the growth of NSCLC cell lines possessing activated ACK1, which often have RAS mutations. (R)-9b induced G2/M arrest and robust cellular senescence primarily in the sensitive RAS mutant NSCLC cell lines; these effects were confirmed with ACK1 knockdown. (R)-9b significantly inhibited the growth of both cell line-derived and patient-derived NSCLC xenografts with RAS mutations in vivo. Mechanistically, ACK1 inhibition suppresses topoisomerase 2A (Topo IIα; encoded by TOP2A) expression, along with downregulation of the expression of gene sets associated with the regulation of DNA repair and replication, resulting in accumulation of DNA damage and subsequent cellular senescence. Overall, RAS mutation in NSCLC cell lines activates the Cdc42/ACK1 axis, conferring sensitivity to ACK1 inhibition that causes accumulation of DNA damage via inhibition of Topo IIα and DNA repair, G2/M arrest, and eventual cellular senescence in RAS mutant NSCLC cells.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Birth plans aim to promote respectful, woman-centered maternity care. However, evidence remains limited regarding whether maternal psychological outcomes are associated with birth plan use, the extent to which the plan is respected, and obstetric complications. OBJECTIVES: To examine whether birth plan use and respect are associated with perceived obstetric violence, post-traumatic stress symptoms, and risk of postpartum depression, and whether these associations differ according to birth type. DESIGN: Cross-sectional questionnaire study. SETTING(S): Spain, 2023. PARTICIPANTS: 2367 women aged ≥18 years who were between one and six months postpartum. METHODS: Participants completed an anonymous online questionnaire. Birth plan status was classified as no birth plan, birth plan not respected, or birth plan respected in most aspects. Analyses were stratified by normal or complicated birth. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for maternal age, attendance at antenatal education, family income, parity, and previous caesarean section. RESULTS: Overall, 1382 women (58.4%) had prepared a birth plan: 370 (15.6%) reported that it was not respected and 1012 (42.8%) that it was respected in most aspects. In bivariate analyses, women whose plans were not respected had the highest prevalence of perceived obstetric violence (normal birth: 35.2%; complicated birth: 45.3%), post-traumatic stress symptoms (25.9% and 40.5%, respectively), and postpartum depression risk (22.2% and 42.1%). Women whose plans were respected had the lowest prevalence of these outcomes. After adjustment, birth plan disrespect was strongly associated with perceived obstetric violence following normal births (adjusted odds ratio: 9.72, 95% confidence interval: 4.42-21.39) and complicated births (adjusted odds ratio: 7.99, 95% confidence interval: 5.60-11.40). papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Healthcare systems face increasing pressures that drive interest in task-shifting to advanced practice nurses, a strategy supported by substantial evidence and reforms in many countries. Belgium recently formalized role expansion of advanced practice nurses through legislation that authorizes defined diagnostic, treatment, prescribing, and coordination activities within collaborative agreements. OBJECTIVE: This study investigates physicians' attitudes toward task-shifting from physicians to advanced practice nurses, identifies perceived barriers to such task-shifting, and maps current and potential areas in which task-shifting may occur. Additionally, the study explores physicians' views on the added value of collaborating with advanced practice nurses. DESIGN: Online cross-sectional survey. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: 634 hospital-based physicians. METHODS: Quantitative and qualitative data were collected using a self-developed questionnaire between May and June 2025. The survey comprised six sections addressing respondents' background, collaboration with advanced practice nurses, knowledge of and attitudes toward the recent legislation, and views on potential task-shifting across eight regulated activities. Analyses were conducted in IBM SPSS Statistics (version 30). Descriptive statistics included frequencies and percentages for categorical and Likert-scale items. Binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with positive attitudes toward task-shifting. Open-ended responses were analyzed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase framework. RESULTS: Among physicians, 18.8% reported being well informed about the new legislation, and 79.9% anticipated impacts on patient care. Overall, 56.9% rated the legislation positively, with less favorable views in dermatology and anaesthesiology. The regression model showed that medical domain and current collaboration with an advanced practice nurse were significantly associated with a positive attitude toward the legislation. The activities most frequently shifted to advanced practice nurses are patient anamnesis and the coordination of referrals to physicians within the same discipline and to other healthcare providers. In future, more than half of physicians (between 54.5% and 77.2%, depending on discipline) indicated a willingness to reallocate six of the eight surveyed activities. Most frequently reported barriers related to perceptions of physician-exclusive tasks, whereas financial concerns and doubts about advanced practice nurses' added value were least reported. Physicians perceived advanced practice nurses as contributing most to improved care quality, addressing unmet needs, and enhancing efficiency. CONCLUSIONS: Most physicians find the new task-shifting legislation positive and believe advanced practice nurses can enhance care quality, address unmet needs, and improve efficiency. However, several barriers remain, highlighting the need for clearer information, defined roles, and robust frameworks for training, liability, and financial arrangements. REGISTRATION: Not registered.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Digital health applications offer scalable support for weight loss, but individual outcomes and retention vary substantially. It remains unclear how predictive information evolves during treatment, whether app engagement adds predictive information beyond early weight response, and whether the same factors predict weight loss and retention. METHODS: Using real-world data from the 12-week digital health application Oviva Direkt for Obesity, we developed machine learning models to predict clinically meaningful weight loss, continuous relative weight change, and full app retention. Weight-change and full-retention analyses included 17,953 and 26,714 adults, respectively. Models evaluated baseline characteristics, 4-week weight, and weekly app engagement metrics separately and in combination to quantify their incremental predictive value and assess how performance changed when early-treatment information was added to pretreatment characteristics. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics alone showed limited discrimination for clinically meaningful weight loss at weeks 8 and 12 (ROC AUC 0.54-0.58). Adding 4-week weight substantially improved performance (ROC AUC 0.86-0.92), whereas app engagement alone yielded modest improvements (ROC AUC 0.63-0.67). Adding app engagement to models including 4-week weight provided little further improvement (ROC AUC 0.87-0.92). A similar pattern was observed for continuous weight-change prediction. In contrast, full-retention prediction improved from ROC AUC 0.81 with baseline characteristics to 0.90 with app engagement, while 4-week weight provided no additional benefit. Weight-loss prediction was driven primarily by baseline weight, 4-week weight, and self-defined target weight, whereas engagement-related variables like goal setting and personalized logging recommendations were more influential for full retention. CONCLUSIONS: Predictive performance for weight-loss outcomes improved substantially when information from the first four weeks, particularly 4-week weight, was incorporated. Accordingly, the week 8 and week 12 models should be interpreted as predictions updated during treatment rather than predictions based solely on pretreatment characteristics. Weight-loss response and sustained intervention use were characterized by distinct predictive information and may require different forms of early, targeted support. These findings provide a basis for further research on the early identification of individuals at risk of suboptimal outcomes and the development of more personalized digital obesity care. External validation in independent, relevant cohorts is required before the models can be considered for clinical implementation.

CONCLUSIONS: Systemic corticosteroid use was significantly associated with an increased risk of tendino-myopathy, which persisted for up to 14 days after discontinuation. papers.abstract_en: Targeted insertion of large DNA fragments has been constrained by the genotoxicity associated with double-strand breaks (DSBs) and the limitations of two-step recombinase systems. Three independently developed mammalian platforms, Quadruple pegRNA (QuadPE), Prime Assembly (PA), and PRIME-In, now achieve programmable, DSB- and recombinase-free insertion of up to 26 kb, 11.3 kb, and 9.2 kb, respectively, through convergent yet mechanistically distinct flap-guided integration strategies. papers.abstract_en: Excessive intake of free sugars is a major modifiable risk factor for obesity, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, and it is a global public-health priority to reduce dietary sugar while preserving sensory quality. Referred to here as "healthy sugars", the low-calorie monosaccharides D-allulose and D-tagatose combine sucrose-like sensory and bulking behavior with a distinct metabolic fate in humans and, for D-tagatose, with defence-inducing activity in plants. This review traces the evolution of sugar supply through four stages, from agricultural extraction of sucrose (Sugar 1.0) and enzymatic hydrolysis to high-fructose syrup (Sugar 2.0) to chemically synthesized high-intensity sweeteners (Sugar 3.0) and precision biomanufacturing of healthy sugars (Sugar 4.0). We review the molecular basis of healthy-sugar action in mammalian metabolic homeostasis and in plant sweet immunity, then compare manufacturing platforms, equilibrium-limited enzymatic epimerization, immobilized-enzyme and continuous-reactor processes, thermodynamically driven cell-free cascades, and cell-free CO2-to-hexose synthesis, through a consolidated cross-platform comparison of conversion, titer, yield, scalability and technology readiness. We then set out an amyloplast-targeted compartmentalised design for sugar-crop chassis, a distinct phosphorylated route for D-tagatose, and a climate-adaptive sugarcane, sugar beet, sorghum manufacturing crops. Finally we examine the conditions under which a plant-chassis route could offer cost or carbon advantages, comparing feedstock, energy, separation and carbon-balance considerations across platforms, and comparing the ingredient and biosafety requirements applying in the United States, the European Union and China. The plant-chassis route is presented throughout as a design proposal requiring crop-level validation, and the prerequisites for its projected advantages are stated explicitly.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: While AI has existed for decades, the introduction of generative AI tools and subsequent advancements in their capability and public use resulted in a shift in public awareness and perceptions of AI. In response, the research community has grown increasingly interested in understanding public perceptions of AI use in various contexts, including health care. Public perceptions shape AI acceptance and consequently integration into health care. It is thus crucial to understand public trust in AI and perceptions of risk as we consider its implementation moving forward. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) document the extent of what is known within the literature regarding public perceptions of AI applications in health; (2) interrogate existing definitions and theories of trust being used to guide investigations of public trust in AI; and (3) identify practice and policy considerations and support the design, deployment, and regulation of these technologies in a manner that is trustworthy. METHODS: The Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines were used to review publications between 2022 and 2024 across 4 databases, resulting in the inclusion of 41 papers for review. Key findings were then charted and organized into tables to help answer the proposed research questions. RESULTS: Public trust in AI in health care was shaped by discourse relating to AI performance and concerns related to depersonalization, loss of human connection, privacy, bias, and transparency. Trust was found to be higher when AI was supporting rather than replacing health care professionals and was influenced by emotional responses, anthropomorphism, demographic factors, and institutional trust. Furthermore, trust extended beyond algorithms to software interfaces, providers, developers, and governing institutions, highlighting the importance of governance and oversight. Conceptualizations of trust varied widely, and trust was defined through vulnerability, competence, benevolence, and integrity. Different theories identified suggested that trust operates across individual, social, institutional, and technological levels. Finally, trust was closely linked to risk and uncertainty, where perceived risk reduced acceptance, while AI literacy, transparency, and explainability mitigated concerns and fostered trust. CONCLUSIONS: Trust in AI is not uniform, and as such, efforts to build and measure trust must account for these nuances to effectively mitigate risk and support informed, ethical AI integration and deployment. On the basis of the findings of this review, we propose a multilevel conceptual framework that provides a general understanding of public trust in AI within a health care context that may guide research and policy and practice considerations. Our findings highlight the importance of considering public trust when implementing AI in health care and may support AI communication strategies, policy development, and trustworthy AI development.

papers.abstract_en: Impact of nutrition on systemic health is well-recognized but the specific sensors that couple western dietary lipid metabolites into the pathological triggers of chronic itch and inflammation remain elusive. Here, we identify a metabolic- to-sensory axis in which 9-keto-12,13-epoxy octadecenoic acid (EKODE), an endogenous dietary linoleic acid derivative acts as a potent ligand for the G protein-coupled receptor 35 (Gpr35) to drive chronic itch, inflammation, and heat hypersensitivity. We demonstrate that Gpr35 is selectively expresses in a distinct population of sensory neurons and genetic ablation of Gpr35 in sensory neurons attenuates EKODE and psoriasis-associated itch and inflammation. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of Gpr35 significantly attenuates itch in mouse models of psoriasis and atopic dermatitis. We show that Gpr35 signaling engages the itch-specific brain natriuretic peptide, defining a labeled-line pathway that is functionally distinct from classical nociceptive circuits. Collectively, our findings establish Gpr35 as a critical neuro-metabolic sensor in healthy and disease conditions.

papers.abstract_en: Enhancer editing is widely proposed as a strategy to modulate gene dosage therapeutically. EKLF/KLF1, a master erythroid transcription factor, is an attractive target because haploinsufficiency is benign and associated with hereditary persistence of fetal hemoglobin (HPFH). Here we test whether enhancer disruption can recapitulate this state by targeting two KLF1 regulatory elements, EHS1 and INT1. EHS1 editing reduces KLF1 expression and increases γ-globin, and combined INT1/EHS1 targeting produces additional increases in some samples, although responses are variable. In xenotransplantation models, edited cells engraft and retain indels but fail to sustain consistent γ-globin induction. Epigenetic profiling across the KLF1 genetic locus reveals a remarkable resistance to loss of hypersensitive sites. These results establish a key principle: the transcriptional consequences of enhancer editing are strongly constrained by local genomic architecture. Attempts to mimic KLF1 haploinsufficiency by non-coding indels are blunted by dense regulatory architecture, enhancer redundancy, and long-range interaction. Thus, it may be difficult to develop KLF1 as a target for gene therapy for hemoglobinopathies until tools for recapitulating natural mutations via heterozygous edits are developed. Our findings underscore the observation that disruption of non-coding elements may not always recapitulate the biology of haploinsufficiency from heterozygous loss-of-function mutations.

papers.abstract_en: The blastocyst formation rate of human embryos cultured in vitro for assisted reproduction is approximately 50%, with most embryos arresting at the cleavage stage; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of biopsied blastomeres from morphologically high-quality 8-cell embryos and tracked the developmental progression of the remaining embryos to the blastocyst stage. Embryos that failed to form blastocysts exhibited impaired zygotic genome activation (ZGA). We identified OVOL1/2 as critical ZGA genes that were markedly underactivated in these embryos. Functional analyses in both mouse and human embryos demonstrate that depletion of OVOL1/2 disrupts trophectoderm differentiation via ARPC1B-dependent mechanisms, thereby impairing the morula-to-blastocyst transition. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insights into preimplantation embryonic development and reveal potential causes of blastocyst formation failure.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nodulosis-arthropathy-osteolysis (NAO) syndrome is an MMP2-related disorder within the multicentric osteolysis, nodulosis, and arthropathy spectrum. Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) involvement is rarely characterized. CLINICAL PRESENTATION: A woman with genetically confirmed NAO syndrome underwent TMJ imaging from 2018 to 2026 while receiving annual intravenous zoledronic acid for systemic skeletal disease. Baseline panoramic and cone-beam computed tomography imaging showed bilateral condylar flattening, cortical thinning, surface irregularity, altered trabecular architecture, and temporal-component involvement. Serial panoramic radiographs demonstrated progressive bilateral remodeling, including erosive changes, articular-eminence flattening, and shallow glenoid fossae. She reported occasional joint sounds without pain, locking, or interference with daily function. Examination showed mild left crepitus, no tenderness or deviation, and maximum comfortable, unassisted, and assisted openings of 36, 37, and 38 mm, respectively. No TMJ-directed treatment was undertaken. CONCLUSION: Progressive TMJ osseous change may occur in NAO syndrome despite minimal symptoms. Imaging should be interpreted with pain, function, examination, and differential diagnosis rather than used alone to establish a temporomandibular disorder or justify treatment.

papers.abstract_en: Lignocellulosic resources are naturally renewable, low-priced, and abundant. They comprise three kinds of polymers, cellulose, hemicelluloses, and lignin, bonded to each other with the help of covalent cross-linking and non-covalent forces. Cellulose is the world's most abundant organic material and the chief constituent of biomass energy. Moreover, production of calluses from Bacillus valezensis strain 2H was statistically optimized by substrate carrot in submerged fermentation using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The RSM and ANN were used to successfully optimize Carboxymethyl cellulase (CMCase) and Filter paper (FPase). Moreover, RSM was utilized for optimization of the target enzyme using a newly identified Bacillus velezensis strain. Plackett-Burman design (PBD) was adopted for screening of the most significant factors affecting cellulase production. Central composite design (CCD) was utilized to optimize enzyme production. Biochemical characterization revealed that both enzymes were optimally active under acidic conditions (pH 6.0), with the optimum temperature observed to be 60 °C, and stability was maintained up to 60 °C. The tested metal ions affected CMCase and FPase activities to varying degrees but did not enhance enzyme activity compared with the control. Similarly, the tested organic solvents generally decreased enzyme activities, although the extent of inhibition varied depending on the enzyme and solvent. R2 values for the CMCase were 95.43% and for FPase 99.58%, calculated by RSM analysis. R2 values for CMCase were 91.44% (Overall R = 0.95622), and for FPase were 53.70% (Overall R = 0.7328), calculated by ANN analysis. Our results showed that the RSM and ANN models provided different predictive performances for CMCase and FPase. This study elucidates the potential of Bacillus velezensis for efficient cellulase production under optimized submerged fermentation conditions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Individual placement and support (IPS) is an effective vocational rehabilitation programme for people with mental illness. This article analyses national policies that directly promote IPS and broader employment-related policies on mental health in 13 European countries. ANALYSIS: IPS alone cannot address the broader workplace and policy conditions that influence sustainable employment. Therefore, creating mentally healthy working conditions also requires action by employers, healthcare systems, and policymakers. POLICY OPTIONS: Recurring barriers and facilitators were identified across countries, alongside variation in governance and implementation contexts. IPS services often operate in isolation, with limited access to consistent training, data, and cross-sector coordination. A national infrastructure for IPS is therefore needed to offer implementation support, intersectoral collaboration should be strengthened and employers need to be supported to advance equity, diversity and inclusion. IPS practice will benefit from policies addressing poor mental health conditions in the workplace, and policies endorsing a recovery-oriented mental healthcare system. CONCLUSION: IPS can build a solid bridge between mental healthcare and employment when integrated into recovery-oriented services and supported by policies that promote inclusive, mentally healthy workplaces.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: IL-33 is a chromatin-associated alarmin of the IL-1 cytokine family involved in tissue homeostasis and immune responses following epithelial or endothelial injury. Although the IL-33/ST2 axis is an attractive therapeutic target, clinical outcomes with IL-33- or ST2-directed agents have varied across diseases and patient populations. AREAS COVERED: This review examines IL-33 biology and the clinical development of tozorakimab, itepekimab, astegolimab and emerging multispecific antibodies across COPD, asthma, atopic dermatitis, food allergy, diabetic kidney disease and viral pneumonia. Particular attention is given to IL-33 oxidation, RAGE/EGFR-associated signaling, soluble ST2, tissue compartment, therapeutic modality and trial design, and to the distinction between pathway activation and pathogenic dependence. EXPERT OPINION: IL-33 remains a promising but context-dependent therapeutic target. Phase 3 COPD trials provide the strongest evidence, particularly for tozorakimab, whereas outcomes with other agents and indications remain inconsistent. Future development should define disease- and endotype-specific dependence on IL-33, clarify the relevance of ST2-independent signaling and soluble ST2, and validate predictive biomarkers using form-resolved assays. Structural differences among anti-IL-33 antibodies may also influence activity, but comparative clinical evidence is lacking. Multispecific approaches may broaden efficacy, but their advantages over established biologics remain to be demonstrated and require prospective evaluation in biomarker-defined patient populations.

papers.abstract_en: Over 100 million Americans carry an estimated $220 billion in medical debt, contributing to two-thirds of personal bankruptcies. Since 2022, state and local governments have responded by purchasing and canceling residents' medical debt. In this scoping review, we examine and compare the structure and impact of these medical debt relief efforts. In sum, 10 states and 21 local governments have eliminated $13.5 billion in medical debt for 7 million residents to date. However, we found that these efforts have been primarily funded by temporary federal pandemic relief dollars that expire after 2026. North Carolina is a notable exception: by conditioning enhanced hospital Medicaid payments on the adoption of debt-mitigation policies, the state has erased $6.5 billion in medical debt among its residents, representing 48% of all relief nationally, without utilizing federal pandemic funds or general state-fund appropriations. We argue that leveraging payment incentives may potentially offer a more durable approach to relieving existing debt and that pairing retrospective debt relief with structural consumer protections is vital to target the upstream drivers of future debt burden. We also argue that sustaining progress requires evaluating program costs and the understudied health and financial outcomes of beneficiaries.

papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: Lichen-associated Cystobasidiomycetes have been reported from a wide range of lichens worldwide. Previous studies proposed that lichen-associated Cystobasidiomycetes may be involved in the development of the thallus cortex, suggesting also a contribution to the construction of thallus architecture within the Parmeliaceae. However, Parmeliaceae do not include species with ecorticate thalli. In contrast, Arthoniales encompass a wide diversity of thallus growth forms, including both corticate and ecorticate types, making this order a suitable model to test this hypothesis across a broader evolutionary context. Furthermore, Cystobasidiomycetes have not yet been studied in Arthoniales. This study aims therefore to (1) characterize the diversity of Arthoniales-associated Cystobasidiomycetes; (2) investigate their selectivity with respect to mycobiont partners and the ecological factors shaping their distribution, and (3) test whether their distribution is consistent with a proposed role in cortex formation and thallus architecture in Arthoniales. The ITS region of Cystobasidiomycetes was sequenced from 169 lichen samples (in majority Arthoniales) and an exhaustive maximum-likelihood phylogeny, including our sequences and all sequences found in GenBank, was inferred using IQ-tree. The effects of substratum, climate, host taxonomy and geographic location on the distribution of Cystobasidiomycetes were assessed using variation partitioning. Cystobasidiomycetes were found in 60 of our samples. Our sequences belonged to 39 Cystobasidiomycetes OTUs, 21 of which were detected in Arthoniales thalli, and eight of them represent unknown lineages. Globally, OTU selectivity was variable. However, most OTU's exhibited a preference for particular groups of mycobionts. Mycobiont taxonomy emerged as the primary factor shaping lichen-derived Cystobasidiomycetes community composition. Climate and substrate likely also influence their distribution, although their effects may be underestimated, due to an unbalanced dataset, dominated by sequences from extra-tropical and corticolous specimens. Finally, no evidence was found to support a correlation between Cystobasidiomycetes detection, thallus growth form or cortex presence in Arthoniales. Overall, these results suggest that lichen-derived Cystobasidiomycetes OTUs largely form lineages distinct from those represented by Cystobasidiomycetes from other sources. However, the lifestyle of many sequences remains uncertain because they were obtained through environmental sequencing. Despite their generally low selectivity, a consistent pattern of mycobiont preference was observed across Cystobasidiomycetes orders. This pattern was not associated with thallus growth form or the presence of a cortex.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) represents the most prevalent form of malignant tumor and constitutes a principal cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Conventional therapeutic approaches predominantly induce apoptosis; however, their efficacy is often compromised by the development of drug resistance. Methuosis, a form of regulated cell death distinct from apoptosis, is characterized by aberrant macropinocytosis and the formation of cytoplasmic vacuoles. Aloperine (ALO), a naturally occurring antitumor alkaloid, has been observed to induce methuosis in cancer cells, although its precise molecular targets and mechanisms remain to be elucidated. This study investigated the anti-NSCLC effects of ALO using cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and mouse xenograft models. Through various assays, it was demonstrated that ALO directly interacts with VPS34 at the I760 residue and promotes TIP60-mediated lactylation of VPS34 at K356 and K781. This interaction inhibits VPS34 kinase activity and reduces intracellular PI(3)P production. The subsequent decrease in PI(3)P levels impedes Armus endosomal recruitment, disrupts Rab7 cycling, leads to the accumulation of macropinosomes, and impairs endolysosomal fusion, ultimately inducing methuosis. ALO exhibits significant antitumor efficacy and acts synergistically with cisplatin to co-activate methuosis and apoptosis, all while avoiding noticeable systemic toxicity. Collectively, ALO targets VPS34 lactylation and disrupts Armus/Rab7 signaling. When used in conjunction with cisplatin, it constitutes a safe and effective therapeutic strategy for NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of using a locally hosted large language model (LLM) to generate patient-friendly radiology reports while avoiding cloud transfer of report text. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, 360 chest, knee, lumbar spine, and shoulder X-rays, and shoulder and abdominal ultrasound reports from Dutch primary care were included. Main report sections (n = 359) and conclusion sections (n = 350) were translated into patient-friendly versions using Gemma-3 (12B parameters) and assessed for accuracy and completeness on 5-point Likert scales. Readability was evaluated using text length and Flesch-Douma reading ease (FDRE) scores. Hallucinations were systematically documented. Statistical analyses included Kruskal-Wallis, Wilcoxon signed-rank, and paired t-tests. RESULTS: Patient-friendly conclusions achieved higher median accuracy scores than main reports (5 [Q1-Q3 5-5] vs 4 [3-5]), while completeness scores were high for both sections (5 [5-5]). Compared with original reports, patient-friendly reports were longer (median increase 65 words [48-84], p < 0.001) and had higher FDRE scores (mean increase 54.2 ± 18.8, p < 0.001). Overall, 71.0% of main reports and 96.0% of conclusions met predefined quality criteria (accuracy and completeness ≥ 4), while 48.0% of combined main report and conclusion sections met both quality and readability criteria (FDRE score > 60). Clinically relevant hallucinations occurred in 45 reports (12.5%). CONCLUSION: A locally hosted LLM demonstrated feasibility for generating patient-friendly translations of Dutch X-ray and ultrasound reports while avoiding cloud transfer of data, with better performance for conclusion sections than main reports. However, clinically relevant hallucinations remain a safety concern and indicate the need for clinician oversight and further evaluation before clinical implementation. KEY POINTS: Question Can a locally hosted LLM generate patient-friendly radiology reports while preserving data privacy and maintaining acceptable accuracy, completeness, and readability? Findings A locally hosted LLM generated patient-friendly report conclusions with higher quality scores than main reports, while clinically relevant hallucinations remained an important safety concern. Clinical relevance A locally hosted LLM has potential to generate patient-friendly radiology report translations without external cloud data transfer. Report conclusions appear to be the most promising initial application, although clinician oversight and further patient-centered validation remain essential before clinical implementation.

papers.title_en: Clustering of Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Midlife Forms Trajectories That Affect Heart Aging Biomarker and Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease.
papers.authors: Panthalanickal Vijayakumar A, Wilsgaard T, Schirmer H, Lindekleiv H, Attia ZI, Lopez-Jimenez F, Leon DA, Iakunchykova O et al.

papers.results: 识别出4个聚类：稳定低危（聚类1，n=1604，30.6%）、血脂异常（聚类2，n=1340，25.6%）、高血压（聚类3，n=1476，28.1%）、高危轨迹（聚类4，n=824，15.7%）。δ-age每增加1个SD与MI、卒中及死亡的超额风险中27%~30%相关（校正年龄与性别后）。聚类3与4的临床事件超额风险最大；δ-age的中介比例较小（MI与卒中总效应的4%~8%）且无统计学显著性。
papers.authors_conclusion: 对传统危险因素的联合多变量生命历程聚类识别出临床上可区分的长期心血管风险表型。尽管δ-age提供独立预后信息，但其几乎不能解释慢性高血压、血脂异常或肥胖相关的超额风险，提示δ-age主要是一种并行标志物而非因果中介。
papers.ai_note: 主要终点方向为中介效应，结果为阴性且作者如实报告，但摘要同时以'独立预后信息'强调δ-age的阳性关联，存在次要关联被前置表述的倾向；'每1-SD δ-age与27%~30%超额风险相关'一句的统计学含义（效应量归属与置信区间）在摘要中未交代，无法核验；聚类由K-means数据驱动、簇数与样条形式未见预设或外部验证信息；观察性设计下中介分析依赖无未测混杂假设，摘要未提及敏感性分析；摘要亦未给出各聚类与事件的HR及CI。

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To (1) identify multivariable longitudinal midlife patterns of systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body mass index, and non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol and (2) assess whether electrocardiogram derived heart age acceleration (δ-age) mediates their associations with incident myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, and all-cause mortality. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed 5244 participants from the observational cohort study, the Tromsø Study, who were free of MI or stroke at baseline (Tromsø7, 2015-2016) and attended at least 3 surveys (Tromsø3-7, 1986-2016). Age-standardized risk factor z-scores were modeled with quadratic B-splines and grouped using K-means clustering to identify joint multivariable life-course risk profiles. δ-Age was derived from 12-lead electrocardiograms using a validated neural network. Natural-effects models decomposed hazard ratios between clusters and clinical events (follow-up to 2021) into direct and δ-age mediated components. RESULTS: Four distinct clusters were identified: stable low-risk (cluster 1, n=1604, 30.6%), dyslipidemia (cluster 2, n=1340, 25.6%), hypertension (cluster 3, n=1476, 28.1%), and high-risk trajectory (cluster 4, n=824, 15.7%). Each 1-SD increment in δ-age was associated with 27% to 30% of excess MI, stroke, and death, independent of age and sex. Clusters 3 and 4 carried the greatest excess risk of clinical events, whereas mediation by δ-age was modest (4%-8% of total effect for MI and stroke) and not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: Joint multivariable life-course clustering of conventional risk factors identified clinically distinct long-term cardiovascular risk phenotypes. Although δ-age adds independent prognostic information, it explained little of the excess risk associated with chronic hypertension, dyslipidemia, or obesity, indicating it functions primarily as a parallel marker and not a causal mediator.

papers.results: 总体ICI治疗队列（n=80）单因素分析中IL-6、IL-8、TNF-α升高与更差PFS和OS相关；多因素校正后仅IL-6为PFS独立不良预后因素（adjusted HR=2.66, p=0.042）。OS方面，有限校正后三者仍显著（IL-6 HR=2.67, p=0.050；IL-8 HR=5.00, p=0.049；TNF-α HR=2.61, p=0.037），但因未行多重检验校正属探索性。一线患者（n=57）中仅IL-6预测更差PFS（adjusted HR=5.34, p=0.002）。G12C亚组（n=38）中IL-6和TNF-α与更差PFS/OS相关；G12D亚组（n=16）中IL-17与更短PFS显著相关（log-rank p=0.037）；G12V/A/S/R亚组中无细胞因子具预后意义。
papers.authors_conclusion: 这些发现提示KRAS突变亚型可能与不同的血清细胞因子谱相关。IL-6似乎是PFS的潜在亚型非依赖性负向预后因素，而IL-17可能在G12D肿瘤中具有相关性。这些观察为探索亚型特异性细胞因子靶向策略提供了早期依据，但需在更大规模前瞻性队列中确认。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未声明预设主要终点，结局为多细胞因子×多终点×多亚组的反复比较，仅OS部分作者自认未做多重检验校正，PFS的IL-6结果（p=0.042）同样处在多重比较边界；G12D亚组仅16例、G12C 38例，亚组结论极易过拟合且效能不足，G12V/A/S/R全阴不能排除样本量与效能问题；139例中仅109例有细胞因子数据，缺失机制与是否随机缺失未说明；OS仅称'limited adjustment'，校正变量集不明，IL-6、IL-8、TNF-α间共线性未讨论；无外部验证与校准信息，属假设生成性质。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: KRAS‑mutant non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is heterogeneous, but the subtype‑specific profiles of systemic cytokines and their impact on immunotherapy outcomes remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective study included 139 patients with KRAS‑mutant NSCLC stratified into G12C (44.6%), G12D (21.6%), and other G12 variants (G12V/A/S/R) (33.8%). Serum levels of seven cytokines (IL‑6, IL‑8, TNF‑α, IL‑10, IL‑17, IL‑1β, IL‑4) were available for 109 patients. Associations with progression‑free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using Kaplan‑Meier and Cox regression. RESULTS: Distinct cytokine profiles emerged across subtypes: IL‑10 was elevated in G12C, while IL‑17 was higher in G12D. In the overall ICI‑treated cohort (n = 80), elevated IL‑6, IL‑8, and TNF‑α were associated with worse PFS and OS in univariable analyses. After multivariable adjustment, only IL‑6 remained an independent unfavorable prognostic factor for PFS (adjusted HR = 2.66, p = 0.042). For OS, all three cytokines remained significant after limited adjustment (IL‑6 HR = 2.67, p = 0.050; IL‑8 HR = 5.00, p = 0.049; TNF‑α HR = 2.61, p = 0.037), but findings were exploratory due to not adjusted for multiple testing. In first‑line patients (n = 57), only IL‑6 predicted worse PFS (adjusted HR = 5.34, p = 0.002). Subgroup analysis showed that in G12C (n = 38), IL‑6 and TNF‑α were associated with worse PFS/OS, while in G12D (n = 16), IL‑17 showed a significant association with shorter PFS (log‑rank p = 0.037). No cytokine was prognostic in the G12V/A/S/R subgroup. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that KRAS mutation subtypes may be associated with distinct serum cytokine profiles. IL-6 appeared as a potential subtype-independent negative prognostic factor for PFS, while IL-17 may be relevant in G12D tumors. These observations provide an early rationale for exploring subtype-specific cytokine-targeted strategies, though confirmation in larger prospective cohorts is needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are common toxicities of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but their prognostic implications in older adults remain uncertain. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using SEER-Medicare (2010-2019). We included patients aged ≥66 years with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who initiated ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy from 2015-2017. Follow-up began at treatment initiation and continued until death, Medicare disenrollment, or December 31, 2019. The primary exposure was a clinically meaningful irAE, defined as an irAE diagnosis with evidence of systemic immunosuppressant use and/or treatment delay, or discontinuation. In secondary analyses, we categorized patients as having no irAE, an irAE managed without hospitalization, or an irAE requiring hospitalization. The primary outcome was overall survival. We estimated adjusted survival differences and restricted mean survival time using doubly robust causal inference methods. RESULTS: The cohort included 5,304 patients (mean age, 75 years; 52.7% female; 81.9% White). Clinically meaningful irAEs occurred in 1,807 (34.1%) patients, with a median onset of 3.8 months (IQR, 1.1-9.4). Death occurred in 65.1% of patients with irAEs and 78.7% without irAEs, corresponding to an adjusted absolute survival benefit of 6.6% (95% CI, 5.3%-8.0%) and a 6.5-month gain in restricted mean survival time (95% CI, 5.6-7.4). In secondary analyses, irAEs managed without hospitalization showed the greatest benefit (odds ratio [OR], 0.44; 95% CI, 0.35-0.54), whereas irAE hospitalization was associated with attenuated benefit (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99). CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with advanced NSCLC receiving ICIs, clinically meaningful irAEs were associated with improved overall survival, particularly when managed without hospitalization. These findings highlight the clinical importance of early recognition of immune-related toxicities; irAE-related hospitalization may identify a higher-risk group warranting closer monitoring and supportive care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet reliable biomarkers to predict clinical response remain limited. This study aimed to identify and validate a clinically practical biomarker reflecting neoantigen-driven immunogenicity and associated with ICI efficacy in NSCLC. METHODS: We conducted a multi-phase study integrating unbiased discovery, clinical validation, and preliminary mechanistic exploration. Multi-omics profiling of a prospective NSCLC cohort (n = 28) integrated genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics to identify fibrinogen alpha chain (FGA) as a top candidate. FGA was evaluated by quantitative immunohistochemistry in a training (n = 93) and independent validation (n = 78) cohort of patients with advanced NSCLC treated with ICIs. Multiplex immunofluorescence characterized FGA‑associated immune biology, and in vitro transcriptomic analysis explored transcriptional programs associated with FGA exposure. RESULTS: FGA expression positively correlated with tumor neoantigen expression (r = 0.618, p < 0.001). In the training cohort, high FGA was associated with significantly prolonged progression-free survival (median PFS: 25.8 vs. 5.2 months; adjusted HR = 0.44, p = 0.003) and higher objective response rate (50.0% vs. 30.8%). These findings were confirmed in the independent validation cohort (median PFS: 38.0 vs. 14.4 months; adjusted HR = 0.42, p = 0.017). Exploratory analyses suggested elevated FGA in PD-L1-high tumors and a trend toward prolonged PFS after adjusting for PD-L1 status, though these findings require validation in larger cohorts. Multiplex immunofluorescence revealed significantly higher densities of CD4⁺, CD8⁺, and CD16a⁺ cells in FGA‑high regions (all p < 0.01). Two distinct spatial patterns were identified in both LUSC and LUAD. Pattern I featured direct immune cell infiltration into FGA-enriched regions with closer immune-tumor contact (p < 0.01), whereas Pattern II demonstrated immune concentration within FGA-outlined tumor nests with predominant accumulation on the tumor side. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that FGA exposure was associated with immune activation in both LUSC and LUAD cell lines and additional metabolic reprogramming in LUAD cell lines. CONCLUSIONS: Immunohistochemical assessment of FGA represents a clinically practical biomarker associated with improved outcomes in ICI-treated NSCLC. Preliminary mechanistic exploration suggests that FGA is associated with an immunologically active but histology-dependent tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To develop and externally test a multiparametric MRI habitat-based framework integrating intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH), peritumoral heterogeneity (PTH), and clinical characteristics for predicting intracranial progression in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and de novo brain metastases receiving first-line third-generation (3rd-gen) EGFR-TKI monotherapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and de novo brain metastases who received first-line 3rd-gen EGFR-TKI monotherapy. Patients were assigned to an internal training cohort (n = 90) and an external testing cohort (n = 51). The binary prediction outcome was intracranial progression within 20 months after treatment initiation. Pretreatment contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging, T2-weighted imaging, and diffusion-weighted imaging were analyzed. The index brain metastasis and a 6-mm peritumoral region were segmented, followed by voxel-wise habitat clustering. Habitat-specific radiomic features were extracted and selected to construct ITH, PTH, and combined intratumoral-peritumoral habitat (PITH) signatures. Clinical predictors were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Support vector machine models were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic, decision curve, calibration, and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: A total of 141 patients were analyzed, including 75 with progressive disease (PD) and 66 without PD (non-PD). Multivariable logistic regression identified EGFR mutation subtype (odds ratio [OR] = 2.390, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.187-4.811, P = 0.015) and the maximum diameter of the index brain metastasis as independent predictors (OR = 2.048, 95% CI: 1.204-3.483, P = 0.008). Models based on imaging heterogeneity features outperformed the clinical model overall. The clinical model achieved an AUC of 0.662, while the ITH, PTH, and PITH models achieved AUCs of 0.715, 0.724, and 0.758, respectively. The combined model showed favorable performance (AUC 0.795, accuracy 76.5%, sensitivity 70.4%, and specificity 83.3%). Patients classified by the combined model as high risk had significantly shorter intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS), than those classified as low risk (log-rank P = 0.019). CONCLUSION: The proposed framework integrating ITH, PTH, and clinical features may provide a noninvasive approach for predicting intracranial progression risk and stratifying prognosis in patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with newly diagnosed BMs receiving first-line 3rd-gen EGFR-TKI monotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Torque teno virus (TTV) is a ubiquitous component of the human blood virome and its replication is tightly controlled by the host immune system. TTV levels have therefore been proposed as a surrogate marker of immune competence. In people with HIV-1 infection (PWH), higher TTV levels have been associated with advanced infection. We investigated TTV levels in individuals diagnosed with non-advanced HIV-1 infection. TTV viral load (VL) was compared between primary and chronic infection to assess whether it could reflect immune dysfunction not captured par CD4+ T-cell counts. METHODS: We conducted a monocentric cohort study including adults newly diagnosed with HIV-1 infection. All participants were antiretroviral therapy-naïve with HIV-1 viremia. Individuals with advanced HIV-1 infection were excluded. HIV-1 infection stage was determined using immunoblot-based laboratory staging according to Fiebig classification. TTV DNA was quantified in serum samples using a qPCR assay. Associations with HIV-1 infection stage were assessed using logistic regression analysis. RESULTS: A total of 126 PWH were included. Primary HIV-1 infection accounted for 42.1% of diagnoses and chronic infection for 57.9%. Overall, TTV DNA was detected in 61.1% of participants. TTV detection was more frequent in chronic infection than in primary infection (82.2% vs 32.1%, p<0.0001). Median TTV VL was also higher in chronic infection (4.82 vs 2.65 log copies/mL, p<0.0001), despite comparable CD4+ T-cell counts. In multivariable analysis, HIV-1 VL and TTV VL were independently associated with HIV-1 infection stage. High TTV VL (≥4 log copies/mL) was strongly associated with chronic infection. CONCLUSIONS: In individuals diagnosed with non-advanced HIV-1 infection, TTV levels differed markedly between primary and chronic infection despite similar CD4+ T-cell counts. These findings suggest that TTV VL could reflect alterations in immune competence not captured by conventional immunological markers and may represent an additional biomarker to assess immune status in PWH.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterise and validate disease-specific muscle imaging patterns in distal and myofibrillar myopathies, quantify their diagnostic performance, and develop an imaging-based classification framework incorporating machine learning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Muscle MRI and CT scans from a multicentre national cohort of patients with genetically defined distal and myofibrillar myopathies were retrospectively analysed. The pattern of muscle involvement for each disease entity was described, and its sensitivity and specificity calculated. Supervised machine learning algorithms were trained using muscle scores and imaging-derived features, and their diagnostic performance was compared using balanced accuracy. RESULTS: A total of 165 patients (mean age 48 ± 16 years; 87 men), including 138 molecularly confirmed cases spanning 19 disease genes, were analysed. Overall, 6350 muscles were systematically evaluated. Key findings included early biceps femoris short head involvement in GNE myopathy, "fat pockets" in myotilinopathy, and early flexor hallucis longus involvement in desminopathy. All imaging patterns showed high sensitivity and specificity (from 75 to 100%). Among the tested machine learning models, XGBoost achieved the highest performance, correctly distinguishing among 11 genetic disease entities with a balanced accuracy of 69%. CONCLUSION: Distal and myofibrillar myopathies demonstrate reproducible disease-specific imaging signatures with high diagnostic accuracy. Integration of these imaging biomarkers into a machine learning framework enables systematic prioritisation of likely genetic diagnoses and may facilitate diagnostic work-up in these heterogeneous inherited muscle disorders. KEY POINTS: Question How accurately do muscle MRI patterns distinguish distal and myofibrillar myopathies, and how do imaging features perform in an updated MRI-based diagnostic algorithm? Findings Disease-specific muscle MRI patterns showed high diagnostic accuracy, while XGBoost achieved the highest balanced accuracy among machine learning models for imaging-based disease classification. Clinical relevance Refined muscle MRI patterns provide diagnostically useful imaging biomarkers in distal and myofibrillar myopathies. Their integration into machine learning-based classification models may facilitate precision diagnostics and guide targeted genetic testing.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Error processing, measured via the error-related negativity (ERN), has been associated with alcohol use disorder (AUD); however, most studies investigating this link have been cross-sectional examinations of adult samples. A key empirical question remains regarding whether the ERN represents a risk factor for AUD, a consequence of heavy drinking or the result of a simultaneously occurring third variable (e.g. anxiety). The present study compared baseline ERN amplitude across model-derived drinking frequency classes to evaluate the nature of this association. DESIGN: Longitudinal multisession cohort study of two independent at-risk adolescent samples across a 2-year tracking period. SETTING: University laboratories at the University of Illinois at Chicago and The Ohio State University, United States. PARTICIPANTS/CASES: Adolescents and young adults aged 16-19 years (M = 18.26, SD = 0.82, 67.9% female) with minimal alcohol exposure and established risk factors for AUD, recruited in two independent samples (n = 110; n = 164). MEASUREMENTS: ERN amplitude was measured at baseline using a modified flanker task. Participants self-reported drinking behavior over the past 90 days at baseline and every 3 months up to 24 months post-baseline. Latent class mixed model analyses were performed to classify trajectories of drinking behavior and a multi-variate generalized linear model was conducted to examine the associations with class and ERN activity. RESULTS: Across both samples, increases in binge drinking frequency were associated with blunted (less negative) ERN activity (Sample 1: P = 0.03, ηp 2 = 0.04; Sample 2: P = 0.01, ηp 2 = 0.05). Associations remained statistically significant after accounting for relevant covariates (anxiety, age, sex). SUMMARY: Blunted error-related negativity amplitude appears to be associated with subsequent increases in binge drinking frequency over time.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Circulating eosinophils can be measured inexpensively and reproducibly in routine care. Beyond their role in parasite defense and allergy, blood eosinophilia is now a key biomarker in respiratory medicine: prognostic, predictive, and recognized as a "treatable trait." Its role as a marker of susceptibility, however, is not well defined. METHODS: We conducted a monocentric retrospective hospital-based cohort study at Montpellier University Hospital (France), including all adults hospitalized in 2018 with a complete blood count and without prior respiratory disease. Eosinophil counts were stratified as < 150/mm³, 150-299/mm³, and ≥ 300/mm³. The primary outcome was incident respiratory disease, defined by hospitalization with a respiratory diagnosis (ICD-10 J00-J99) or initiation of inhaled therapy (ATC R03). Follow-up extended to December 2024; secondary outcomes included diagnostic subcategories and ICU admission. RESULTS: Among 24,405 patients, 6,173 (25.3%) developed incident respiratory disease. Event rates followed a dose-response pattern across eosinophil strata: 21.7% (< 150/mm³), 26.0% (150-299/mm³), and 32.9% (≥ 300/mm³; p < 0.001 pairwise comparisons across all groups). After multivariable adjustment, eosinophilia remained independently associated with higher risk of developing respiratory disease (HR 1.45, 95% CI 1.35-1.55). Baseline eosinophilia was also associated to increased ICU admissions and greater disease severity during the follow-up. CONCLUSION: Blood eosinophilia was strongly associated with both increased risk of developing incident respiratory disease and in-hospital severity, in a clear dose-response manner. However, most patients with high counts (> 300/mm3) did not develop respiratory events, underscoring the need to integrate blood eosinophil counts with complementary clinical and biological data for risk stratification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Early diagnosis of paediatric lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in intensive care is difficult because clinical features overlap with non-infectious respiratory failure and conventional microbiology has limited sensitivity. We aimed to integrate airway microbial and host-response signals to identify early diagnostic biomarkers in mechanically ventilated children. METHODS: We re-analysed airway metagenomic sequencing and tracheal aspirate transcriptomics from 261 ventilated paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) patients using differential expression, protein-protein interaction network analysis, and machine-learning feature selection. Findings were evaluated in an exploratory assessment of biologically related cytokine markers within an independent prospective cohort (RASCALS; n = 100 enrolled, n = 78 analysed) using non-bronchoscopic mini-bronchoalveolar lavage (mini-BAL), plasma cytokines, and clinician-adjudicated diagnoses. RESULTS: Respiratory syncytial virus and Haemophilus influenzae were the only pathogens consistently enriched in LRTI. Host transcriptomics showed activation of interferon, cytokine, and chemokine signalling. Network-guided feature selection identified a seven-gene panel (IRF7, FFAR3, GZMB, FABP4, FN1, CXCL5, BCAR1) with high diagnostic performance in cross-validation (median F1 0.94), comparable to a published 14-gene model. In RASCALS, a logistic model using mini-BAL IL-1β, IL-4, and IL-8 classified bacterial LRTI with 65% accuracy (sensitivity 70%, specificity 63%), while blood IL-6 and TRAIL achieved 82% accuracy (sensitivity 79%, specificity 83%). CONCLUSIONS: Integrating airway microbial profiles with host-response biomarkers supports earlier and more specific LRTI diagnostic classification in ventilated children. The seven-gene panel and cytokine combinations are candidates for rapid PCR- or immunoassay-based bedside tests to inform antimicrobial stewardship.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) serve as the standard first-line therapy for advanced EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, resistance inevitably restricts their efficacy. Although well-documented acquired resistance mechanisms have been extensively characterized, approximately 30% of patients with EGFR-TKI resistance still present with unknown resistance (UR) mechanisms, and the driving factors behind primary resistance remain inadequately understood. METHODS: In this study, we conducted a large-scale, retrospective cohort study, performing target-capture deep sequencing (>400 genes) on 928 samples from 745 EGFR-TKI-resistant and 183 TKI-naïve EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. RESULTS: The molecular landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance was systematically characterized. In the resistance cohort, 68.72% (512/745) harbored known resistance (KR) mechanisms, while 31.28% (233/745) were classified as UR. The landscape of KR was significantly influenced by EGFR-TKI generation. First-line third-generation TKI resistance demonstrated fewer EGFR-dependent events compared to first-generation TKIs (p < 0.01) and more RTK and PI3K-AKT-mTOR (PAM) pathway alterations (p < 0.05). In the UR cohort, pathway analysis revealed unique enrichment of atypical pathways, most notably ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling pathways. Differential gene analysis identified significant enrichment of MYC, BRCA1, EPHB, and PTPRD in the UR subgroup. To investigate primary resistance, we found that baseline IKZF1 amplification was significantly enriched in patients with short time-to-treatment-failure (TTF) and correlated with significantly poorer outcomes (HR = 3.02, 95% CI 1.32-6.90; log-rank p = 0.004). CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a comprehensive real-world landscape of EGFR-TKI resistance, demonstrating distinct mechanisms influenced by TKI generation. ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling was identified as a distinctive pathway feature of unknown resistance, and baseline IKZF1 amplification emerged as a candidate biomarker of EGFR-TKI primary resistance. These findings suggest that epigenetic dysregulation may be a critical driver of both unknown and primary resistance to EGFR-TKIs.

papers.abstract_en: In specialized herbivores retaining a carnivorous digestive tract, such as the giant panda, early-life oral microbiome assembly is crucial for lifelong health, yet remains poorly understood. Here, we longitudinally tracked the saliva and supragingival plaque microbiomes of captive cubs (180 matched samples) from birth to one year using microbiome sequencing and topological cartography. We demonstrate a profound spatial-temporal divergence driven by deterministic succession. Initial plaque colonization exhibited transient priority effects reflecting maternal imprints, rapidly superseded by autogenic niche reconstruction and deep anaerobic maturation. Host ontogeny, notably deciduous tooth eruption, triggered intense microbial exchange, causing significant transient habitat homogenization (peak Mantel correlations at months 6 and 8, p < 0.001). Mature plaque selectively enriched for peptidoglycan biosynthesis and complex carbohydrate degradation, establishing a pre-adaptive metabolic reservoir for the impending high-fiber bamboo diet. Crucially, topological analysis (interaction edges expanded 3.4-fold) revealed that early pioneers evade competitive exclusion by shifting their ecological niche to become inter-module connectors (Pi > 0.62), providing spatial scaffolds for late-arriving climax communities. These findings decipher the deterministic assembly rules of saliva and plaque microbiomes during the extreme milk-to-bamboo dietary transition, advancing our understanding of giant panda adaptive evolution and identifying native keystone targets for preventive veterinary interventions.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate longitudinal adoption of American College of Radiology (ACR) Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS) Terminology, report-level documentation of Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) criteria, and associated ultrasound-guided FNA practice in a large multisite radiology network. METHODS: In this retrospective, multicenter study across 89 imaging sites, 304,455 diagnostic thyroid ultrasound reports (CPT 76536) and 11,246 ultrasound-guided FNA reports (CPT 10005/10006) from 2017 through 2023 were analyzed. A linked pre-biopsy cohort of 994 diagnostic reports immediately preceding FNA was examined. Automated text mining identified TI-RADS language and documentation of nodules meeting ACR size-based FNA thresholds. Trends were assessed using Cochran-Armitage, Spearman correlation, and χ2 tests. RESULTS: TI-RADS language increased from 1.6% of thyroid ultrasound reports in 2017 to 54.1% in 2023. Among 112,036 TI-RADS-containing reports, 11,845 (10.6%) documented nodules meeting FNA criteria. This proportion declined from 23.3% in 2017 to 8.0% in 2023, an absolute decline of 15.3 percentage points (Z = -47.94, P < 0.001) and was inversely correlated with annual TI-RADS adoption across the seven annual observations (ρ = -1.000, P < 0.001). Among FNA-indicated reports, TR4 predominated (56.9%), followed by TR3 (21.0%) and TR5 (19.4%); category distribution shifted significantly over time, although the effect size was small (χ2 = 169.91, P < 0.001; Cramér's V=0.086). In the pre-biopsy cohort (n=994), 498 (50.1%) contained TI-RADS language. The FNA rate per 1,000 thyroid ultrasound examination remained stable (29.1 in 2017; 27.7 in 2023). CONCLUSION: ACR TI-RADS terminology use increased substantially but remained incomplete. Increasing terminology use was associated with declining report-level FNA eligibility. Biopsy appropriateness could not be assessed from report-level documentation alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Platinum-etoposide plus a programmed death-ligand 1 inhibitor is standard first-line therapy for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). Febrile neutropenia (FN) is a frequent adverse event. Primary granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) prophylaxis may reduce FN but also modulate antitumor immunity. We examined whether primary G-CSF prophylaxis reduced FN without compromising chemoimmunotherapy efficacy. METHODS: This Japanese multicenter, retrospective observational study enrolled patients with ES-SCLC or relapsed limited-stage SCLC treated with platinum-etoposide plus atezolizumab or durvalumab. The primary endpoint was FN incidence during first-line therapy. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM) were used for primary and sensitivity analyses, respectively. RESULTS: Among 285 patients, 64 received primary G-CSF prophylaxis (pegylated G-CSF administration in cycle 1). In IPTW analyses comparing the primary and non-primary G-CSF prophylaxis groups, the former was associated with lower FN incidence (2.6% vs. 28.6%; odds ratio [OR], 0.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.02-0.30), fewer FN-related emergency visits (1.6% vs. 16.1%) and admissions (1.6% vs. 15.3%), and higher average relative dose intensity (0.76 vs. 0.71). Objective response rate was 65.7% vs. 73.1% (OR, 0.71; 95% CI: 0.36-1.42), median progression-free survival was 4.8 vs. 5.1 months (hazard ratio [HR], 0.88; 95% CI: 0.63-1.22), and median overall survival was 14.2 vs. 13.2 months (HR, 0.79; 95% CI: 0.55-1.13), without any differences between the groups. PSM findings were comparable. CONCLUSIONS: Primary G-CSF prophylaxis during first-line SCLC chemoimmunotherapy was associated with lower FN incidence and FN-related acute-care use, without evidence of compromised antitumor efficacy.

papers.title_zh: 跨年龄单核RNA测序图谱显示早发性结直肠癌以间质比例升高、上皮FN1与长链非编码RNA表达增高及细胞间通讯增强为特征
papers.title_en: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum.
papers.authors: Porter CBM, Murphy SP, Cazaubiel J, Delorey TM, Amir-Zilberstein L, Ashenberg O, Klindziuk L, Andrews E et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Klarman Cell Observatory, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, Cambridge, MA, USA.
papers.results: MSS肿瘤中，年轻患者肿瘤表现为间质成分比例升高、上皮成分比例降低，并在外部712例MSS CRC队列（18例EO，694例AO）中用多光谱免疫荧光与机器学习验证；年轻患者肿瘤上皮细胞长链非编码RNA与FN1表达升高，拷贝数变异异质性呈增高趋势；MSS左侧EO-CRC肿瘤细胞间相互作用更多，上皮-间质转化相关信号通路（FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN）呈现细胞类型特异性相互作用增强。
papers.authors_conclusion: 该大型高分辨率snRNA-seq图谱揭示了结直肠癌的年龄相关特征，并为学界理解EO-CRC生物学提供了资源。
papers.ai_note: ①全文为描述性图谱研究，摘要未给出任何效应量、置信区间或P值，'trend toward increased heterogeneity'为无统计学支持的措辞；②外部验证队列年龄构成极度失衡（EO 18例 vs AO 694例），验证的稳健性与代表性有限；③摘要声称校正部位、分期、性别与新辅助治疗史，但未呈现校正模型与结果，无法判断混杂控制程度；④无生存、治疗反应等临床结局关联，临床转化价值尚属推断；⑤研究主题为结直肠癌，与胸科业务关联度很低。

pico.p: 189例原发结直肠癌肿瘤（54例早发性EO-CRC，诊断年龄<50岁；135例平均发病年龄AO-CRC，≥50岁），覆盖八个十年，多数年龄十年≥20例；外部验证队列712例MSS结直肠癌（18例EO，694例AO）
pico.ic: 按年龄连续或分类（EO vs AO）分层的单核RNA测序图谱分析（并按微卫星状态分层，校正肿瘤部位、分期、性别与新辅助治疗史）；对照为AO-CRC及不同年龄层肿瘤，无干预措施

papers.reason: 该研究提供的是消化道肿瘤的年龄分层单细胞图谱资源，对胸部肿瘤日常诊疗决策无直接影响；其价值在于为'年龄相关肿瘤微环境/上皮比例变化'这一跨瘤种假设提供方法学与对照基线参考，可用于设计肺癌年轻发病患者的单细胞研究，但契合胸科的程度天然较低。
papers.abstract_en: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

papers.title_en: Multi-genome benchmark for simple and complex genome inversion detection.
papers.authors: Cheng S, Sedlazeck FJ
papers.affiliation_highlight: Human Genome Sequencing Center, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, TX, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: 提供首个统一的高分辨率倒位基准，揭示现有方法跨平台的明确优势与局限；该资源为工具有原则的开发、评估与调优奠定基础，使社区能更准确解析倒位变异及其生物学与临床后果。

pico.ic: 评估短读长、PacBio HiFi与Oxford Nanopore数据上的主流结构变异调用器及Minimap2/VACmap长读长比对流程；无临床干预对照
