papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Inversions represent a consequential yet under-characterized form of structural variation, with roles in genomic disorders, evolution, and genome instability. However, their detection remains technically challenging, particularly within repeat-dense regions and for complex multi-breakpoint events. A lack of dedicated, high-quality benchmarks has hindered algorithmic improvement, performance comparison, and robust biological interpretation. RESULTS: Here, we present a multi-genome benchmark for simple and complex inversions derived from Strand-seq and phased long-read based assemblies across five reference samples, with breakpoint refinement using haplotype-resolved long-read assemblies. This tiered resource spans a broad spectrum of inversion classes, sizes, and zygosity states, and captures challenging genomic contexts including segmental duplications, inverted repeats, and composite rearrangements. We use this benchmark to systematically assess leading structural variant callers and alignment strategies across short-read, PacBio HiFi, and Oxford Nanopore data. Performance varies by inversion class and genomic context: simple inversions were recovered with high sensitivity at sufficient coverage, whereas complex and heterozygous events remained difficult. Sniffles2 and Severus achieve the strongest recall for complex inversions, despite increased false-positive rates. We additionally benchmark two commonly used long-read alignment pipelines (Minimap2 and VACmap), demonstrating that the mapper choice has a substantial impact on inversion detection in repetitive regions. CONCLUSIONS: Together, this work provides the first unified, high-resolution inversion benchmark and reveals clear strengths and limitations of current methods across platforms. Our resource establishes a foundation for principled tool development, evaluation, and tuning, enabling the community to more accurately resolve inversion variation and its biological and clinical consequences.

papers.title_en: Influenza virus antagonizes self-sensing by RIG-I to enhance viral replication.
papers.authors: Ledwith MP, Nipper T, Davis KA, Uresin D, Zhang Z, Kleer M, Khaperskyy DA, McCormick C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Medical Microbiology and Immunology, University of Wisconsin Madison, Madison, WI 53706, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: self-sensing is strategically deployed by the cell to amplify the antiviral response and reveal a newly identified viral countermeasure that disrupts RIG-I activation by host RNAs.
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告样本量、具体模型系统及统计数值；标题称增强病毒复制，但摘要主要描述NP拮抗RIG-I对宿主RNA的感知，未直接给出病毒复制增强的定量证据；机制发现与胸科肿瘤临床决策距离较远。

pico.ic: 干预与对照：流感病毒感染下，宿主RNA聚合酶III转录的非编码RNA经RIG-I被感知；流感病毒NP与RIG-I经RNA桥互作并拮抗该感知（摘要未述及具体对照组）

papers.reason: 揭示RIG-I可被宿主非编码RNA激活及流感病毒NP的拮抗机制，影响对呼吸道病毒天然免疫识别的基础认识；对胸外科/胸部肿瘤日常判断无直接影响，仅可作病毒-免疫微环境研究背景参考。
papers.abstract_en: Innate immune sensors must finely distinguish pathogens from the host to mount a response only during infection. RIG-I is a cytoplasmic sensor that triggers a broad antiviral response in response to sensing foreign RNAs. Here, we show that RIG-I not only binds viral RNAs but is activated by host RNAs. These are primarily non-coding RNAs transcribed by RNA polymerase III. They are benign under normal conditions but become immunogenic during influenza virus infection, where they signal via RIG-I to suppress viral replication. These RNAs are also bound by influenza virus nucleoprotein (NP), which normally functions to encapsidate the viral genome. NP interacts with RIG-I via an RNA bridge and antagonizes sensing of self-RNAs to counter innate immune responses. Overall, we demonstrate that self-sensing is strategically deployed by the cell to amplify the antiviral response and reveal a newly identified viral countermeasure that disrupts RIG-I activation by host RNAs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tezepelumab is a monoclonal antibody approved in the United States for severe asthma. Real-world evidence of effectiveness remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of tezepelumab in reducing annualized asthma exacerbation rates (AAERs) and healthcare resource utilization (HRU) in the United States. METHODS: This retrospective, self-controlled, pre-post cohort study used data from Symphony Health, an ICON plc Company, PatientSource®, December 1, 2020, to June 30, 2024. Eligible patients were ≥12 years, had ≥2 records of tezepelumab, and experienced ≥2 asthma exacerbations in the 12 months before tezepelumab initiation, with index date being the day after initiation. AAERs and asthma exacerbation-related HRU were compared between the 12 months pre- and post-index. AAERs were also evaluated across patient subgroups. RESULTS: A total of 527 patients were included. AAERs decreased significantly from 2.81 to 1.26 per person-year (55% decrease; 95% confidence interval [CI] [51%, 59%]; p<0.001). The greatest benefit was observed among patients starting treatment February 2023 and later (61% decrease; [53%-67%]; p<0.001). Consistent reductions were seen across subgroups: patients with pre-index blood eosinophil count <300 cells/μL and ≥300 cells/μL, pre-index total serum immunoglobulin E levels <100 IU/mL and ≥100 IU/mL, biologic-naïve and biologic-experienced, persistent tezepelumab users, and those with comorbid chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis. Asthma exacerbation-related HRU declined significantly (p<0.001) with 50-54% reductions across healthcare settings. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, patients with severe asthma treated with tezepelumab had substantial reductions in asthma exacerbations and HRU, with the greatest benefits among more recent initiators.

papers.title_en: Peri-Infarct Cortical Network Remapping During Stroke Recovery via a Soft Liquid Metal Neural Interface.
papers.authors: Kim E, Kim E, Lee J, Jeong I, Hong YM, Oh M, Lee S, Park JU et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Yonsei University, Seoul, South Korea.
papers.results: Stroke causes substantial reorganization of neural activity and connectivity in the peri-infarct cortex during functional recovery. Tracking these changes at high resolution, however, remains difficult.
papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: Stroke causes substantial reorganization of neural activity and connectivity in the peri-infarct cortex during functional recovery. Tracking these changes at high resolution, however, remains difficult. Mechanical mismatch of conventional rigid neural probes is exacerbated in the fragile peri-infarct region, destabilizing the tissue-electrode interface and limiting long-term recording. Here, we present a fully soft, liquid metal-based multichannel neural interface that enables stable electrophysiological recording in freely moving mice. Using this platform, we performed longitudinal recordings before and after ischemic stroke, enabling within-animal comparisons. We applied complementary analyses of population-level latent dynamics and functional connectivity, capturing network-level coordination and pairwise interactions. Both analyses revealed acute suppression followed by partial recovery without restoration of the pre-stroke state. Instead, neural networks reorganized into a distinct and reproducible functional configuration. These findings establish soft liquid metal neural interfaces combined with population-level analysis as a useful approach for resolving neural reorganization during stroke recovery.

papers.abstract_en: MXenes, a family of two-dimensional (2D) materials known for their characteristic electrical, optical, and surface properties, have emerged as promising candidates for advancing the performance of photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensing technologies. When integrated into composites, including carbon-based materials, metal nanoparticles, and conductive polymers, MXenes' intrinsic properties, such as high surface area, high electrical conductivity, and tunable surface chemistry, can contribute to improving the sensitivity, selectivity, and stability of PEC biosensors. These characteristics make MXenes suitable for applications across various sectors, such as healthcare, food safety, and environmental monitoring. This review comprehensively outlines the core principles of PEC sensing, highlighting the role of MXene-based composites and light-driven processes in facilitating the detection of miRNA, protein biomarkers, small biomolecules, drug molecules, pesticides, and organic contaminants. It further explores recent advancements in MXene composites for detecting a broad spectrum of biological targets in complex biological samples. The review also addresses challenges, including the requirements for stability, reproducibility, biocompatibility, and scalability in various practical applications. Finally, it discusses future perspectives on MXene-integrated composites for PEC biosensing and their potential applications in clinical diagnostics, precision medicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

METHODS: Data were collected on all confirmed measles cases that were evaluated at one of the emergency departments (ED) in the three main hospitals in Jerusalem from the first reported case of the current outbreak on April 10th to December 31st, 2025. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were analyzed using robust Poisson multivariable models to calculate incidence rate ratios (IRR) for hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and death. RESULTS: Among 786 individuals who visited the ED with confirmed measles, the rates of hospital admission (≥1 day), ICU, ECMO and death were 83.4%, 6.4%, 0.8%, and 1.4%, respectively. Complete data were available for 567 patients, of whom 303 (53.4%) were males. Median age was 2.1 years (IQR 1.2-3.8), and 474 (83.6%) were younger than 5 years. Most patients were unvaccinated (91.0%). Secondary infections were frequent, including lobar pneumonia (28.7%) and community-acquired bacteremia (3.5%). Respiratory support and severe dehydration were associated with hospital admission (IRR 1.4, 95% CI 1.3-1.5; p<0.001 and 9.5, 4.8-18.4; p<0.001, respectively) and ICU admission (IRR 1.3, 1.2-1.4; p<0.001 and 5.2, 2.1-12.4; p<0.001, respectively). Community-acquired bacteremia was associated with death or ECMO (IRR 44.5, 12.5-158.6; p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Despite high access to medical care in this urban setting, measles caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Respiratory compromise, severe dehydration, and bacteremia identified patients at increased risk of severe outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Atmospheric new particle formation (NPF) contributes to aerosol number concentrations and their contribution to cloud condensation nuclei. However, the relative roles of species such as sulfuric acid (H2SO4), ammonia (NH3), and biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) in regulating particle formation and growth are not well understood in urban environments. To address this gap, continuous in-situ measurements of NH3, BVOCs, and particle number size distributions were conducted between June 2023 and January 2024 at the Thissio urban background site in Athens, Greece. H2SO4 concentrations were also estimated with an advanced proxy method. The period-mean NH3 concentration was 2.3 ± 0.7 μg m-3, with warm-season variability consistent with air-mass transport from surrounding agricultural areas. NPF occurred on 19% of measurement days and exhibited the highest frequencies (29‒33%) in autumn, when atmospheric ventilation was reduced and the condensation sink was lower, while enhanced growth rates were observed in summer. Limited variability in H2SO4, NH3, and BVOCs was observed between event and non-event days, indicating that single-precursor abundance alone cannot explain NPF occurrence. The highest formation rates (J at 14 nm) were calculated under intermediate NH3 and H2SO4 concentrations together with relatively low BVOC levels, highlighting the combined influence of precursor availability, condensation sink (CS), and cluster survival. In contrast, gaseous precursors exhibited clearer relationships with particle growth, with higher growth rates occurring under enhanced NH3 and BVOC (isoprene and monoterpene) availability. Our findings emphasize that NPF occurrence under urban Eastern Mediterranean conditions is not exclusively determined by precursor abundance, condensational losses, and particle survivability, but rather by a combination of these factors, while BVOCs show a clear association with subsequent particle growth.

papers.abstract_en: Adoptive cellular therapies depend on the adequate expression of target antigens on tumors. The disialoganglioside GD2, a target of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells (GD2.CAR T cells) and monoclonal antibodies, is variably expressed in Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma. We investigated the ability of chromatin-directed small molecules to enhance tumor GD2 and sensitize tumors to GD2.CAR T cells. Although the EZH2 inhibitor tazemetostat increased GD2 levels in culture and in xenografted mice, tazemetostat treatment was unable to maintain sufficient tumor GD2 levels necessary to enable tumor control in a metastatic xenograft model. We performed a screen of chromatin-directed small molecules to identify additional compounds capable of regulating tumor GD2 and identified multiple compounds, including the HDAC inhibitor entinostat and the DOT1L inhibitor pinometostat. Both compounds greatly enhanced tumor GD2 expression by tazemetostat in culture but did not limit CAR T-cell activity. In multiple xenograft models, the combination of tazemetostat and entinostat resulted in enhanced tumor GD2 expression and led to long-term tumor control by GD2.CAR T cells. These data offer preclinical support for the incorporation of chromatin-directed inhibitors into ongoing CAR T-cell trials for Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma.

papers.abstract_en: Hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA), an alternative to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), can cross the placental barrier, raising concerns regarding fetal hepatic development; however, the mechanisms underlying its developmental hepatotoxicity remain poorly elucidated. Here, human embryonic stem cell-derived hepatocyte-like cells (HLCs) were exposed to HFPO-TA at 3, 15, or 75μM for 28 days during hepatocytic differentiation. HFPO-TA accumulated intracellularly in a dose- and time-dependent manner and impaired hepatic function, evidenced by reduced albumin secretion and CYP activity and increased alanine transaminase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling revealed extensive disruption of lipid metabolism, including increased triglycerides, total cholesterol, and low-density lipoprotein levels, and decreased high-density lipoprotein levels. HFPO-TA activated PPAR signaling and altered genes and proteins associated with lipid synthesis and oxidation, with significant perturbations even at the environmentally relevant concentration of 3 μM. Oil Red O staining and altered PLIN1 and PLIN2 expression confirmed lipid droplet accumulation. HFPO-TA also disrupted mitochondrial function, altered respiratory chain activity, reduced ATP production and mitochondrial membrane potential, and up-regulated fission-fusion-related genes. Collectively, these findings indicate that HFPO-TA impairs hepatocyte differentiation through PPAR-mediated lipid remodeling and mitochondrial dysfunction, highlighting safety concerns for this PFOA alternative. Furthermore, HLCs are a valuable in vitro model for assessing the developmental toxicity of PFOA alternatives.

papers.abstract_en: Rechargeable lithium-ion batteries (LiBs) are central to the clean energy transition, but their production, use, and disposal may introduce contaminants into drinking water systems. Using U.S. EPA Fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR5) data, we evaluated whether ZIP codes with LiB waste activity or LiB facilities had higher lithium or per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) burdens in drinking water. LiB waste activity was identified from the 2023 EPA Biennial Hazardous Waste Report, and LiB facilities were identified from the NAATBatt Lithium-Ion Battery Supply Chain Database. Among 17,860 ZIP codes, 254 had LiB waste activity and 633 had at least one LiB facility. In adjusted conventional regression models, waste presence (β = -0.464, 95% CI: -0.919, -0.010) and facility presence (β = -0.491, 95% CI: -0.786, -0.196) were inversely associated with lithium concentrations, but these associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in spatial-error models. PFAS findings were mixed. Waste presence was not associated with summed PFAS concentration (β = -0.051, 95% CI: -0.175, 0.073), while shipped waste tonnage showed a borderline positive association (β = 0.259, 95% CI: 0.000, 0.518) that was attenuated after spatial adjustment. In spatial-error models, facility presence (β = 0.067, 95% CI: 0.015, 0.120) and facility count (β = 0.086, 95% CI: 0.026, 0.146) were positively associated with summed PFAS concentration. Overall, associations were sensitive to spatial dependence and varied across LiB indicators. These exploratory findings do not establish that LiB activities caused PFAS contamination but suggest that LiB facility locations warrant further investigation as indicators of industrial environments with elevated or more complex PFAS contamination.

papers.abstract_en: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection. DESIGN: Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis. SETTING: Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection. INTERVENTIONS: Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations. MEASUREMENTS: CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. MAIN RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations. CONCLUSIONS: Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.

papers.abstract_en: Direct compression (DC) is an attractive route for tablet manufacturing, yet its impact remains constrained by the poor flowability of many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and the high excipient loading required for reliable compaction. Here, we introduce a microfluidic particle engineering approach that co-processes API with polymeric excipients to produce highly flowable microparticles with tuneable compaction behaviour. Notably, excellent tabletability is achieved with minimal excipient loading, thereby addressing both critical requirements of DC. Using a parallelized step-emulsification device, monodispersed droplets containing dissolved naproxen (NPX) and ethyl cellulose (EC) were fabricated and subjected to antisolvent extraction to produce spherical co-processed microparticles. Robust tablet tensile strength exceeding 5 MPa was achieved with only 11% excipient loading - enabled by a self-assembled core-shell structure featuring an EC-rich shell encapsulating an NPX-rich core. Moreover, adjusting the API-to-excipient ratio produced microparticles with distinct morphologies and solid-state outcomes, resulting in greater tabletability with higher excipient loading. Overall, the microfluidic platform approach allows for a systematic study of self-assembled particle structures produced by API-excipient co-processing and their impact on DC formulations.

papers.abstract_en: The minimally invasive delivery of therapeutics across biological barriers is a major challenge in modern medicine. Microneedles (MNs) are novel platforms to address this challenge effectively. Simultaneously, the therapeutic potential of live microorganisms has been harnessed for various biomedical applications. The integration of living microorganisms with MNs has recently emerged as a promising strategy that combines minimally invasive delivery with dynamic biological functions. This review explores the integration of different microorganisms (probiotics, commensal bacteria, pathogenic and engineered bacteria, and microalgae) into MNs for various biomedical applications such as chronic skin conditions, wound dressing, cancer therapy, and intradermal vaccination. In preclinical studies, these platforms generally showed improved outcomes compared with free microorganisms, microorganism-free MNs, or conventional treatments used as controls. Furthermore, combining microorganisms with photothermal agents, sonosensitizers, antibiotics, and nanozymes can further enhance therapeutic performance. Synergistic mechanisms in these platforms - such as targeted pathogen killing, microenvironment remodeling (hypoxia alleviation and glucose consumption), and in situ generation of gases and metabolites - highlight their potential as a new class of localized therapies. Finally, the current challenges along with the future potential applications of these emerging platforms are discussed in detail.

papers.abstract_en: Drug-drug cocrystals offer a promising strategy for developing fixed-dose combination formulations by integrating multiple active pharmaceutical ingredients into a single crystalline lattice. However, their application may be limited by insufficient dissolution improvement and the relatively large particle sizes of conventional cocrystals. Herein, an imatinib-curcumin drug-drug nanococrystal (nano-IM-CUR) was prepared by combining cocrystallization with nanonization to investigate its apparent dissolution behavior and pharmacokinetic performance following intravenous administration in rats. A wet-milling strategy assisted by magnetic stirring was established, and formulation and process parameters were systematically optimized. The optimized nano-IM-CUR exhibited an average particle size of approximately 200 nm, a narrow size distribution, and good reproducibility. Solid-state characterization confirmed that the original cocrystal phase was retained after nanonization. Compared with the micron-sized cocrystal, nano-IM-CUR exhibited higher apparent plateau concentrations of IM and CUR under the tested non-sink dissolution conditions. The nanococrystal suspension showed limited changes in particle size and PDI during 180 days of storage at 4 and 25 °C under the tested conditions. Following intravenous administration in rats, both IM and CUR were detected in plasma. This study provides an equipment-accessible wet-milling strategy for converting the micron-sized IM-CUR drug-drug cocrystal into a nanosized suspension while retaining its characteristic cocrystal phase.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for detecting clinically suspected hip abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients after total hip arthroplasty and to evaluate the association between specific MRI features and surgically confirmed tears. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 36 patients with total hip arthroplasty who underwent revision surgery for a suspected abductor tendon tear and had preoperative MRI available. Intraoperative findings served as the reference standard for the presence of partial or full-thickness tears of the gluteus medius (Gmed) and gluteus minimus (Gmin) tendons. Two readers evaluated MRI for tendon integrity (intact, partial-thickness, or full-thickness tear). Associations between tendon defects, peritrochanteric fluid, tendon signal abnormalities, and Gmed/Gmin Goutallier grades with surgical findings were analyzed using regression models to calculate odds ratios (ORs). RESULTS: For detection of abductor tendon tears, Reader 1 achieved sensitivities of 0.86-1.00, specificities of 0.93-1.00, and accuracies of 0.92-0.97, while Reader 2 achieved sensitivities of 0.86-1.00, specificities of 0.90-1.00, and accuracies of 0.89-1.00. Imaging findings associated with partial- or full-thickness tears included tendon defects (Gmed: OR = 35.5, p = 0.007; Gmin: OR = 30.0, p < 0.001), peritrochanteric fluid (Gmed: OR = 64.2, p = 0.01; Gmin: OR = 74.9, p = 0.01), and higher Goutallier grade (Gmed: OR = 2.34, p = 0.03; Gmin: OR = 4.75, p = 0.02). CONCLUSION: MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting surgically confirmed hip abductor tendon tears in this selected symptomatic surgical cohort following total hip arthroplasty. Tendon defects and peritrochanteric fluid were significantly associated with partial- or full-thickness tendon tears. KEY POINTS: Question There is limited data on the diagnostic accuracy of MRI for hip abductor tendon tear detection following total hip arthroplasty. Findings MRI demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy for detecting surgically confirmed abductor tendon tears in symptomatic patients with total hip arthroplasty. Clinical relevance In symptomatic patients with clinical suspicion of an abductor tendon tear undergoing evaluation for revision surgery, MRI can be used to noninvasively assess the integrity of the abductor tendons after total hip arthroplasty.

papers.abstract_en: Major trauma is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly among children and young adults, and rapid identification of life- or limb-threatening injuries through imaging is crucial. Whole-body CT (WBCT) is central in modern major trauma pathways, enabling early detection of critical findings to guide multidisciplinary decision-making. Our study suggests three evidence-based recommendations for WBCT in major trauma care. First, WBCT protocol selection should be tailored to haemodynamic status and injury mechanism rather than applied as a single universal protocol; incorporating split-bolus, dual-phase and triple-phase techniques, each offering different diagnostic strengths and trade-offs. Special considerations can apply in pregnancy, paediatric patients, and those with contrast allergy, who may require modified imaging strategies. Second, radiologists should play an active role in trauma multidisciplinary team (MDT) care, assisting in protocol adaptation and directly directing the trauma team to life-threatening injuries. Third, systematic, checklist-driven radiological reporting with defined communication pathways improves trauma diagnostics, increases reporting reproducibility and strengthens trauma decision-making. These recommendations are best implemented through locally agreed, mechanism and physiology-based WBCT protocols, supported by trauma-trained radiologists embedded in scanning processes and multidisciplinary trauma care. KEY POINTS: Whole-body CT enables rapid and comprehensive assessment of patients with major trauma and suspected multisystem injury. Radiologists play an active role in trauma team care through real-time CT assessment and early identification of life-threatening injuries. Modern trauma imaging should incorporate standardised, protocol-driven acquisition and structured image interpretation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The United States Prescribing Information (USPI), also known as the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) drug label, serves as a primary source of information for healthcare professionals to access reliable information on drug benefits and risks. Within the drug label, adverse events are listed across varying sections (e.g., Contraindications, Warnings and Precautions, Adverse Reactions). However, at present it is unclear what evidentiary thresholds FDA applies before including specific adverse event types in various sections of the drug label. To examine this question, we conducted an analysis of United States (US) regulations, guidance documents, standard operating procedures and policies published by FDA pertaining to the assessment of adverse events and drug labeling. OBJECTIVE: This study examines how causality assessments shape decisions regarding the inclusion and placement of adverse events in the US drug label. METHODS: We analyzed US regulations and policy documents published by FDA up to June 2024. Sources included the electronic Code of Federal Regulations, FDA policy documents (e.g., guidance documents, standard operating procedures, and policies) identified through searches of the FDA website and Westlaw legal database. Documents were analyzed using ATLAS.ti to extract and compare causality-related language across drug labeling sections. RESULTS: Our analysis identified heterogeneous and sometimes contradictory causality assessment evidentiary thresholds across US drug label sections. We found no predefined or standardized causality thresholds specified in FDA regulations, allowing interpretive flexibility that may contribute to variability and opacity in labeling decisions. For example, the Adverse Reactions section requires "some basis to believe" a causal relationship, while the Warnings and Precautions section states that "reasonable evidence" of causality is needed for serious events. CONCLUSION: We recommend greater standardization of causality-related terminology and public documentation of evidentiary rationales supporting labeling decisions. Improved clarity regarding evidence certainty would better support prescribers and patients in understanding drug-related harms and strengthen public trust in regulatory drug safety assessments.

We examined the performance of mCIM and eCIM among CRE-encoding NDM, OXA-48-like, or both. Isolates included Escherichia coli (53.5%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (41.3%), and Enterobacter species (5.3%). Overall, 112 isolates (65.1%) encoded NDM alone, 23 (13.4%) encoded OXA-48-like alone, and 37 (21.5%) encoded both NDM and OXA-48-like. mCIM positivity was 98.2% for NDM, 47.8% for OXA-48-like, and 94.6% for NDM+OXA-48-like encoders; among mCIM-positive isolates, eCIM positivity rates were 99.1%, 91%, and 97.1%, respectively. When compared to molecular carbapenemase gene detection, mCIM/eCIM was highly sensitive for classifying isolates encoding NDM as metallo-β-lactamase (MBL) producers, but significantly misclassified isolates encoding OXA-48-like as having an MBL or lacking a carbapenemase. In the largest collection of NDM and OXA-48-like co-encoding CRE isolates to date, mCIM/eCIM typically reported these as MBL producers. IMPORTANCE: Carbapenemase-encoding Enterobacterales infections are associated with substantial adverse health outcomes, making rapid and accurate carbapenemase detection essential for guiding antibiotic therapy. Although Enterobacterales carrying multiple carbapenemases are increasingly reported worldwide, the performance of common phenotypic assays, mCIM and eCIM, remains insufficiently defined for these strains. In this study of 172 genotypically confirmed carbapenemase-encoding Enterobacterales isolates from hospitalized patients in South India, mCIM/eCIM consistently classified NDM-encoding isolates as metallo-β-lactamase encoders. Additionally, mCIM/eCIM frequently misclassified OXA-48-like-encoding isolates as either metallo-β-lactamase encoders or carbapenemase-negative, highlighting the need to better understand the mechanisms underlying this variable activity. In the largest collection of NDM and OXA co-encoding Enterobacterales isolates reported to date, mCIM/eCIM generally reported co-encoding isolates as metallo-β-lactamase producers. Our results suggest that mCIM/eCIM performance may vary geographically due to variable activity, distribution, and combinations of carbapenemases.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a common chronic liver disease with significant clinical burden. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of embryonic stem cell-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ESC-MSCs) in cellular and murine models of MASLD. METHODS: HepG2 cells were treated with palmitic acid (PA) and then co-cultured with ESC-MSCs. C57BL/6 mice were fed a choline-deficient, L-amino acid-defined, high-fat diet (CDAHFD) or a standard diet for 24 weeks. Either ESC-MSCs or vehicles were administered via tail vein injection at week 20. Lipid accumulation was assessed using Oil red O staining. Mitochondrial status was assessed using MitoTracker Red fluorescence, mtDNA content, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and antioxidant parameters. RESULTS: ESC-MSC co-culture reduced PA-induced lipid accumulation, restored mitochondrial activity, decreased ROS, and increased superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and glutathione redox balance. Expression of phosphorylated AMPK (p-AMPK), PGC1α, and PPARα was significantly upregulated. In CDAHFD-fed mice, ESC-MSC transplantation attenuated hepatic steatosis, restored mitochondrial DNA content, and reduced ROS accumulation with increased SOD activity and glutathione ratio. Hepatic expression of p-AMPK, PGC1α, and PPARα was also enhanced. These effects were abrogated by Compound C, an AMPK inhibitor. ESC-MSCs secreted hepatocyte growth factor (HGF), which activated AMPK, suggesting an HGF-AMPK axis may serve as a potential paracrine mechanism. CONCLUSION: ESC-MSCs ameliorated hepatic steatosis in MASLD models by restoring mitochondrial activity and reducing oxidative stress, possibly involving HGF-associated AMPK pathway modulation. These findings support the potential of ESC-MSC therapy for MASLD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a chronic, life-limiting genetic disease. Treatment with CFTR modulators (CFTRm), such as the triple combination therapies elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ELX/TEZ/IVA) and vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (VNZ/TEZ/D-IVA), have significantly improved clinical outcomes and quality of life for many people with CF. While most individuals treated with CFTRm report no change or improvement in neuropsychiatric symptoms, a minority have reported new or worsening symptoms. This has led to hypotheses that CFTRm or CFTR function could have relationships to neuropsychiatric symptoms. METHODS: To evaluate potential off-target or on-target effects of CFTRm and/or CFTR function on neuropsychiatric symptoms, we conducted four independent analyses: (a) in vitro off-target screening at clinically-relevant free concentrations; (b) nonclinical, in vivo behavioral pharmacology studies; (c) analysis of clinical trial and real-world evidence of CFTRm neuropsychiatric adverse events; and (d) human genetic analysis of CFTR functional variants in ∼1 million individuals diagnosed with neuropsychiatric disorders. RESULTS: No off-target effects of ELX, VNZ, TEZ, or IVA were observed in vitro at clinically-relevant free concentrations, nor were any behavioral findings observed in vivo animal studies. Up to date analysis of clinical trial and real-world data covering >250,000 patient-years of experience with CFTRm did not show any increase in risk of neuropsychiatric adverse events. Human genetic analyses of functional CFTR variants did not identify association with any of 23 neuropsychiatric conditions. CONCLUSIONS: Multiple independent lines of investigation failed to show any evidence for off-target or on-target effects of CFTRm and/or CFTR function on neuropsychiatric symptoms.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: The Galα1-3Galβ1-4GlcNAc-R (αGal) epitope is found in all non-primate mammals, lemurs, and New World monkeys, but not in Old World monkeys, apes, or humans. Humans possess natural anti-αGal antibodies, which are hypothesized to prevent virus spillover through neutralization and complement-mediated inactivation of glycosylated viruses carried by animal hosts. Low or absent titers of anti-αGal antibodies are found in newborns and certain populations, leading to a reduced natural antibody-mediated immune barrier. The expression of αGal in animal reservoirs of coronaviruses remains unclear. Surprisingly, the α-1,3-galactosyltransferase (α1,3GT) gene in pangolins is classified as inactive according to the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Reference Sequence: XM_036915461.1. In this study, we cloned the α1,3GT family from animal reservoirs of coronaviruses and investigated its ability to modify surface glycoproteins of the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) pseudovirus. The results showed that the bat and pangolin genomes contain functional α1,3GT1 and α1,3GT2 genes. The bat α1,3GT1 can catalyze the expression of the αGal epitope on SARS-CoV-2 envelope glycoproteins. Anti-αGal antibodies neutralized SARS-CoV-2 pseudoviruses packaged in glycoengineered 293T cells expressing the αGal epitopes. Our findings reveal the presence of functional α1,3GTs in animal reservoirs of coronaviruses, which may be exploited as a target for natural antibody neutralization to prevent virus spillover. papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Current evidence supports the associations between diet, intestinal microbiome, and colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, but their causal relationships have not been extensively determined. Using large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets of gut microbes (18,340 individuals), food preference (161,625 individuals), and CRC (24,476 cases vs. 23,073 controls), we applied a phenome-wide two-step bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) study to evaluate the causal effects of 45 food-liking traits on CRC susceptibility, and the mediating role of 131 microbiota. The inverse variance weighted (IVW) method was primarily employed, followed by multiple sensitivity analysis to assess the validity of the results. Among 45 categories, fatty/salty food preference was suggestively associated with a decreased risk of CRC [odds ratio (OR)IVW 0.65, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43-0.98, p = 0.040]. Furthermore, we identified four distinct food-microbiota association pairs, along with nine bacteria-CRC pairs. By integrating the association pairs, a putative causal pathway was found in dairy preference, increased abundance of Faecalibacterium (dairy preference-Faecalibacterium: βIVW = 0.72, 95% CI 0.30-1.13, p = 6.87 × 10-4), and decreased CRC risk (Faecalibacterium-CRC: ORIVW 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.97, p = 7.05 × 10-3), among which Faecalibacterium served as a potential mediator (p mediation = 0.035). Subsequent stratified analysis showed a consistent mediation in late-onset (age > 50; p = 0.029) and female (p = 0.049) populations. Our findings uncovered a novel causal pathway of dairy preference, gut Faecalibacterium levels, and CRC susceptibility, providing additional insights into CRC etiology and early prevention of CRC through dietary interventions. papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Systematic literature reviews are widely acknowledged to be at the top of most evidence hierarchies but are very time-consuming and labour-intensive. The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) offers possibilities to accelerate the review process. We propose a systematic literature review protocol that incorporates AI and evaluate the accuracy of AI against a human-constructed gold standard. Human researchers performed a systematic literature review on the PubMed metabolomic literature investigating Long COVID. OpenAI model o3-mini was then used via the application programming interface to carry out the three key stages of a systematic literature review: 1) screening articles for inclusion criteria, 2) evaluating articles' risk of bias (RoB) using a customised metabolomics tool based on well-established quality criteria, and 3) extracting data from articles. The performance of AI was evaluated against a manually created reference by the assessment of accuracy, negative predictive value, precision, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and Cohen's kappa. Out of the 320 identified articles, 33 met all inclusion criteria. AI performed screening, RoB assessment, and data extraction with mean accuracies of 92.7% ± 4.9%, 91.9% ± 5.9%, and 92.0% ± 9.2%, respectively, in ~ 10 h and at a cost of ~ 15.35 USD, while human reviewers took ~ 116 h, equivalent to ~ 2000 USD at minimum wages, to complete these steps in duplicate. OpenAI model o3-mini can independently complete the three main stages of systematic literature reviews in the metabolomics domain, thus considerably reducing the time to complete such reviews, at minimal cost. Nonetheless, human reviewers should always verify the AI-generated output to ensure robustness. papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) entails a health burden associated with a higher risk of organ ischemia and mortality, which can cause postoperative complications, such as acute kidney injury (AKI) or myocardial injury (MI). However, there is no unified definition of IOH, and the evidence regarding the association between IOH under different definitions and postoperative complications is still limited and uncertain. We searched PubMed, Web of Science and Embase databases from inception to December 24, 2024 and conducted an evidence map and a systematic review. To further confirm the threshold of IOH and explore the relationship between the duration of IOH and AKI/MI, we conducted sub-analyses by threshold of IOH, and dose-response meta-analyses based on the most commonly used threshold. A total of 81 studies involving 686,153 participants were included. We found that the publication rate of IOH and AKI/MI studies has been increasing in the last 10 years. In total, 52 unique studies were included for AKI and 12 studies were included for MI. The corresponding odds ratios (ORs) were 1.10 [95% Confidence Interval (CI), 1.08-1.12] and 1.27 (95% CI, 1.07-1.50), respectively. We further conducted sub-analysis by definition of IOH. The pooled ORs for AKI among mean arterial pressure (MAP) < 65 mmHg, MAP < 60 mmHg, MAP < 55 mmHg and systolic blood pressure (SBP) < 90 mmHg were 1.09 (95% CI, 1.04-1.13), 1.04 (95% CI, 1.00-1.07) , 2.22 (95% CI, 1.37-3.60) and 1.10 (95% CI, 0.99-1.23), respectively. The pooled ORs for MI among MAP < 65 mmHg, MAP < 60 mmHg, and SBP < 90 mmHg were 1.22 (95% CI, 0.95-1.57), 1.17 (95% CI, 1.08-1.27), and 2.17 (95% CI, 0.48-9.81), respectively. When the threshold of IOH was 65 mmHg, there was a linear relationship between IOH and AKI. For every 10-minute increase, the risk of AKI in patients with IOH was 12% higher than the risk in patients without IOH. IOH is significantly associated with increased risks of postoperative AKI and MI, with stronger effects at lower MAP thresholds. The linear relationship between IOH duration and AKI risk highlights the need to minimize IOH. Targeted hemodynamic management strategies are essential to reduce postoperative complications, especially in high-risk patients. papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Elevated temperatures, including warm ambient temperature (WAT) and high ambient temperature (HAT), profoundly influence plant growth and development. While WAT promotes thermomorphogenesis and stimulates growth, HAT induces stress responses that can inhibit growth. Using Arabidopsis thaliana, we uncovered both shared and distinct molecular mechanisms underlying plant responses to these temperature conditions. We demonstrated that both WAT and HAT activate genes associated with the DNA damage response (DDR), but they differ in timing and intensity. While WAT encourages progression into the S phase of the cell cycle and enhances cell division, HAT induces G2/M arrest, indicating cell cycle inhibition caused by DNA damage accumulation and impaired DDR proteins. Notably, alternative splicing (AS), particularly intron retention (IR), emerged as a pivotal regulatory layer under heat stress. Prolonged high temperatures uniquely enriched IR events in genes involved in DNA repair and chromatin organization. Integrated analyses of AS and transcriptional changes revealed coordinated regulation, with IR events dominating genes that exhibit simultaneous upregulation. These findings highlight AS as an essential regulatory mechanism in plant responses to heat stress. Conserved responses to elevated temperatures in tobacco and tomato further suggest the presence of shared adaptive pathways across plant species. Our results provide novel insights into plant adaptation to fluctuating temperatures and highlight opportunities for engineering heat-resilient crops to mitigate the impacts of climate change. papers.abstract_en: Neonicotinoid insecticides, such as thiamethoxam (TMX), are widely used in agriculture, but concerns over their potential hepatotoxicity, particularly in the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MASLD), persist. This study investigates the role of hepatic nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT) in TMX-induced liver damage, focusing on its impact on lipid metabolism and liver injury. Chronic TMX exposure upregulated NNMT expression in the liver and primary hepatocytes, leading to increased lipid accumulation and oxidative stress. Depletion of hepatic NNMT in liver-specific knockout (LKO) mice significantly attenuated TMX-induced hepatic steatosis, hyperlipidemia, and liver injury. The protective effects were associated with suppressed de novo lipogenesis, reduced oxidative stress, and alleviated endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, suggesting a critical role of NNMT in these processes. Further mechanistic studies revealed that NNMT depletion restored the activation of adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), a key regulator of lipid metabolism. These findings demonstrate that hepatic NNMT plays a pivotal role in the development of TMX-induced MASLD and highlight the potential of NNMT inhibition as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate TMX-related liver damage. Our results underscore the complex role of hepatic NNMT in metabolism and propose its inhibition as a promising intervention for preventing and treating liver-related metabolic disorders, especially in populations at high risk of pesticide exposure.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is the third most common malignancy associated with Lynch syndrome (LS). Various guidelines endorse universal germline testing in patients diagnosed with UTUC. We evaluated the utilization of germline testing in UTUC using a nationwide claims database. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We queried the MarketScan database for patients with newly diagnosed UTUC between January 2015 and June 2023. The primary outcome was receipt of germline testing, defined as claims for multigene hereditary cancer panel testing after diagnosis. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify independent associations of testing. RESULTS: Of 4,783 patients with newly diagnosed UTUC, 216 (4.5%) patients underwent germline testing, with no meaningful change across the study period. On multivariable analysis, prior Lynch-spectrum cancer was independently associated with germline testing (odds ratio [OR], 3.00 [95% CI, 2.14 to 4.22]), as was male sex (OR, 1.37 [95% CI, 1.01 to 1.86]). Northeast residence was associated with lower odds of postdiagnosis testing compared with the South (OR, 0.54 [95% CI, 0.34 to 0.85]). Among patients diagnosed before age 50 years, a stand-alone criterion for genetic evaluation, only 5.6% underwent germline testing. LS diagnosis after UTUC diagnosis was ultimately claimed in eight patients across the entire cohort. CONCLUSION: Germline testing in UTUC is performed in fewer than 1 in 20 patients and remains low even in patients meeting established clinical criteria for evaluation. Structural integration of germline evaluation into upper tract urothelial carcinoma care pathways is needed.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Influenza virus replication relies on coordinated assembly of ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes in the nucleus, yet how host long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify the lncRNA AL645608.7 as a potent antiviral factor and show that its two splice variants restrict influenza replication. Mechanistically, AL645608.7 contains eight tandem 66-nt repeats that recruit the RNA-binding protein PTBP1, primarily through PTBP1's RRM3 domain. The AL645608.7-PTBP1 assembly then engages key viral RNP components-PB2 and NP-and functionally disrupts the PB2-NP interface, thereby suppressing viral RNA synthesis. Domain-mapping analyses further distinguish the regions responsible for PTBP1 recruitment from those involved in PB2 and NP engagement, demonstrating that distinct structural elements of AL645608.7 coordinate host-protein recruitment and viral RNP interference. Importantly, lipid nanoparticle delivery of AL645608.7 markedly reduces viral burden and improves disease outcomes in mice, providing a proof-of-concept nucleic-acid therapeutic strategy. Together, our findings reveal a repeat-programmed lncRNA mechanism that rewires a host RNA-binding protein to dismantle influenza RNP organization and support the therapeutic potential of lncRNA-based intervention against influenza virus infection. IMPORTANCE: This study identified that influenza virus infection significantly upregulated the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) AL645608.7. Both of its transcripts, AL645608.7-v1 and AL645608.7-v2, exhibited antiviral activity against influenza virus. Mechanistically, AL645608.7 was shown to directly bind to the host protein PTBP1. Furthermore, the nuclear-localized AL645608.7 recruits PTBP1 via a 66-base repeat motif. Importantly, PTBP1 interacts with both the N- and C-terminal regions of the influenza virus polymerase subunit PB2 as well as the NP, thereby disrupting the NP-PB2 interaction. The AL645608.7-PTBP1 complex amplifies this inhibitory effect, ultimately impairing vRNA synthesis and blocking efficient viral replication. These findings offer novel insights into the functional role of noncoding RNAs in host-influenza virus interactions.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Malaria remains one of the major threats to human health. Breakthrough drugs with high potency and low resistance risk are needed to combat the ever-increasing resistance to currently deployed antimalarials. Here, we explore a series of 4-aminoquinazoline-based sulfonamides (4AQS), with a synthetically accessible scaffold. Exemplars exhibit nanomolar potency against blood stage Plasmodium cultures, with up to 300-fold selectivity compared with a mammalian cell line. The compounds are active against transmissible stages of Plasmodium falciparum and refractory to resistance development. Targeted mass spectrometry reveals that the 4AQS compounds act as reaction hijacking inhibitors targeting P. falciparum aminoacyl tRNA synthetases (aaRSs). Subtle changes to the chemical structure switch the main target from cytoplasmic threonine tRNA synthetase (PfThrRS) to cytoplasmic asparagine tRNA synthetase (PfAsnRS), a change that is associated with increased potency against P. falciparum. The target preference was confirmed by selective knockdown of different P. falciparum aaRSs and by tolerance selection in a mutator line. Consistent with aaRS targets, exemplar compounds activate the amino acid starvation response. Recombinant enzyme inhibition and thermal stabilization assays confirm the susceptibility of PfAsnRS to reaction hijacking and show that human AsnRS is less susceptible. A molecular model of Asn-tRNA-bound PfAsnRS reveals that a potent hijacker adopts a pose similar to adenosine 5'-monophosphate (AMP). An AlphaFold model of the native PfAsnRS dimer helps explain the tolerance-conferring effect of a mutation at the dimer interface. IMPORTANCE: Every year, at least 200 million new malaria infections are diagnosed, causing more than 600,000 deaths in Africa and Southeast Asia. Ever-increasing levels of resistance to current antimalarials are leading to an impending crisis. Breakthrough drugs with new modes of action are much needed. Here, we explore a series of inhibitors that hijack critical malaria parasite enzymes. The target enzymes catalyze the formation of a bond between the hijackers and an enzyme substrate, forming a tight-binding compound that disrupts the malaria parasite's protein translation machinery. The hijacking inhibitors exhibit high-level potency against the disease-causing stage of the malaria parasite and are also active against transmissible stages. They exhibit up to 300-fold selectivity compared with a mammalian cell line, possess drug-like chemical attributes, and are easily synthesized. Importantly, the compounds are refractory to resistance development.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: High pressure (HP) can trigger bacterial spore germination, acting either through germinant receptors (GRs) or the SpoVA channel. However, the mechanism by which HP activates these membrane-embedded proteins remains elusive. Here, using Bacillus subtilis, we demonstrate that the GerA GR is the primary target of moderate HP (50-300 MPa). Mutagenesis reveals that pore-lining residues within the GerA ion channel are essential for the pressure response, whereas canonical ligand-binding and intramembrane signaling residues are dispensable. We then propose a stretch-to-open (STO) model, in which HP differentially compresses the more compliant inner membrane (IM) relative to the rigid spore core, generating lateral membrane tension that promotes the opening of the GerA channel. In situ membrane tension measurements indicate HP-induced compression of IM phospholipids and elevated membrane tension. This tension-dependent gating is further supported by the pressure-dependent phenotypic rescue of GerA channel mutants. Consistently, HP increases IM permeability to water-soluble and membrane-impermeable agents (propidium iodide and formaldehyde), an effect potentiated by GerA, indicating concomitant opening of GerA by HP. Furthermore, modulating IM fluidity via heat activation or decoating altered membrane physical properties and delayed HP-induced germination, establishing the IM as the critical mechanical transducer. Additionally, computational modeling and calculations support faster compression of the IM than of the core under HP, rationalizing the source of tensile stress. Together, our findings establish a novel mechanism of HP-induced GerA activation via the STO model: HP compresses the IM, generates lateral tension, and promotes opening of the GerA ion channel to trigger bacterial spore germination. IMPORTANCE: Bacterial spores are notoriously resilient, posing significant challenges to health and industry. While high pressure is known to trigger spore germination, the biophysical mechanism has remained elusive. Here, we provide evidence that high pressure mechanically activates the germinant receptor GerA via a "stretch-to-open" mechanism. Because the inner membrane is highly compressible compared to the rigid spore core, pressure induces membrane compression that generates lateral tension. This tension promotes opening of the GerA ion channel. Our study identifies the inner membrane as a critical mechanical transducer, addressing a long-standing question in spore biology and suggesting a distinct mechanosensory adaptation involved in spore revival.

papers.abstract_en: Aspergillus fumigatus is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen and an important cause of invasive aspergillosis in immunocompromised patients. Azole antifungals remain central to treatment, but azole resistance is increasingly reported. Azole resistance in A. fumigatus is often linked to canonical cyp51A mechanisms, but many resistant isolates lack these mutations, suggesting additional contributions. This study analysed 12 newly sequenced azole-susceptible clinical isolates from KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, together with publicly available clinical and environmental A. fumigatus genomes using a uniform AF293 reference-based workflow for variant calling, population structure correction and genome wide association studies (GWAS). A filtered SNP-alignment matrix was used to infer population structure and perform structure-aware genome-wide association testing with azole susceptibility status as a binary phenotype. Overall, 194 of 227 genomes met predefined quality thresholds, and 31 949 biallelic SNPs were tested using ten PCoA axes as covariates. After adjustment using SNP-derived PCoA covariates, 16 SNPs exceeded the Bonferroni threshold and 206 SNPs passed BH-FDR correction. The strongest association signals were distributed across multiple genomic regions rather than being restricted to a single canonical resistance locus, with candidate annotations linked to sterol and lipid metabolism, membrane transport, transcriptional regulation, cell-wall remodelling and stress response. Transporter-focused analysis showed that all 12 South African isolates had negative CDR1 and MFS transporter-balance scores, placing them among the most transporter-depleted susceptible backgrounds in the dataset. Phylogenetic reconstruction showed interspersed resistant and susceptible isolates, supporting repeated emergence or local amplification rather than expansion of a single resistant clone. Overall, these findings support a cautious model in which azole resistance-associated variation in A. fumigatus is distributed across multiple functional pathways within a structured population background. The South African isolates provide a local susceptible clinical baseline for future expanded surveillance.Keywords: Aspergillus fumigatus, Azole resistance, Genome Wide Association, SNPs.

papers.abstract_en: Fusarium head blight (FHB), caused by Fusarium graminearum, is a globally significant fungal disease affecting wheat and barley crops. Chemical fungicides remain the primary control method. However, fungicide resistance remains a big challenge. This study assessed the sensitivity of field populations of F. graminearum from the Huang-Huai-Hai wheat region of China to the triazole fungicide propiconazole. All 101 isolates collected were sensitive, exhibiting EC50 values ranging from 0.0210 to 0.4520 µg/mL with a mean of 0.1740 µg/mL. The unimodal frequency distribution of EC50 values indicated no detectable resistance, establishing these values as a baseline sensitivity for monitoring regional F. graminearum populations. To evaluate the resistance risk, four propiconazole-resistant F. graminearum laboratory mutants were characterized. Stability testing across generations (1st, 3rd, 7th, and 10th) cultured without fungicide confirmed stable inheritance of the resistance phenotype. Evaluation of the biological fitness revealed significant (p < 0.05) reductions in mycelial growth, sporulation, and pathogenicity in resistant mutants, although the spore germination rate increased. Molecular analysis of the CYP51 genes (FgCYP51A, FgCYP51B, and FgCYP51C), encoding sterol 14α-demethylase that target propiconazole, identified multiple point mutations conferring amino acid substitutions, including A101T, E102G, V104I, S168G, D247N, and G251R in FgCYP51A, V31A, and N272D in FgCYP51B and E164K, S256A, M273T, V307A, and V424E in FgCYP51C. Gene expression analysis showed consistent up-regulation of FgCYP51A and down-regulation of FgCYP51B and FgCYP51C in resistant mutants. Meanwhile, the study demonstrated cross-resistance between propiconazole and the demethylase inhibitor (DMI) fungicides prochloraz and difenoconazole. However, there is no cross-resistance between propiconazole and tebuconazole, difenoconazole, fluazinam, and carbendazim, this provides a basis for resistance management strategies such as rotating applications or mixing fungicides with different modes of action.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Enterococcus faecium (E. faecium) co-harboring the vanA and vanM genes is an emerging multidrug-resistant pathogen mediating high-level vancomycin resistance, yet its epidemiological and genomic characteristics remain poorly understood, creating critical knowledge gaps for clinical infection control and the management of high-risk patient populations. Using a clinical isolate from a pediatric patient and publicly available genomes from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) database, this study aimed to elucidate the genomic features, phylogenetic relationships, and genetic context of the resistance gene clusters in vanA- and vanM-positive E. faecium. METHODS: Complete genome sequencing was performed on 24VR2004. Comparative analysis included 97 NCBI-sourced vanA- and vanM-positive genomes. Resistance/virulence genes were analyzed via CARD/VFDB databases; phylogenetic analysis and resistance gene cluster genetic context analysis were conducted. RESULTS: 24VR2004 (ST80, CC17) had vancomycin MIC > 256 µg/mL, 23 resistance genes, 15 virulence genes. Its vanA (intact, Tn1546-M97297.1) and vanM (vanX-in-vanM-cl-deleted, flanked by IS1216E/ISEfa4) were on different plasmids. Among the total 98 isolates analyzed (our clinical isolate 24VR2004 and 97 NCBI-derived genomes), all originated from Asia, with 60.2% recovered from urine samples. ST555 was the predominant sequence type, accounting for 56.1% of the cohort, and strain 24VR2004 was phylogenetically closely related to two ST80 isolates from Guangdong, China. Three complete genomes had plasmid-borne vanA and vanM: two (24VR2004, GCA_053011635.1) on separate plasmids, one (GCA_023658035.1) on one plasmid. vanA clusters in all three were within Tn1546-like transposons (intact in 24VR2004's p24VR2004_P3 and GCA_053011635.1's CP172562.1), while CP058893.1's vanA clusters lacked vanY_in_vanA_cl and vanZ_in_vanA_cl but had a duplicated vanX_in_vanA_cl downstream. All vanM clusters lacked vanX_in_vanM_cl; p24VR2004_P2's vanM clusters had IS1216E upstream and ISEfa4 downstream, others only IS1216E upstream. CONCLUSION: All vanA- and vanM-positive E. faecium isolates included in this study are geographically restricted to Asia, with ST555 as the predominant sequence type. Plasmid-borne dual resistance clusters, mediated by Tn1546-like transposons and IS1216E, drive their dissemination. This study provides preliminary genomic evidence regarding the dissemination and genetic context of vanA- and vanM-positive E. faecium and may support future surveillance and infection control efforts for high-risk populations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Inanimate objects can serve as carriers for the transmission of potential pathogenic bacteria, especially those exhibiting multidrug resistant. Multidrug-resistant bacteria are significantly contributing to healthcare-associated infections. METHODS: Swab samples were collected from 185 inanimate objects using stratified simple random sampling for this cross-sectional study. The Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method was employed to identify the antimicrobial susceptibility of the isolates. After that, SPSS version 26.0 was used to analyze the data, using bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses to evaluate associations. 95% confidence intervals and odds ratios were used to report associations, and p < 0.05 was used as the threshold for statistical significance. S. aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococcus: the majority of bacteria showed multidrug resistance, which presented a serious risk for infections linked to healthcare. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The rumen microbiota is essential to substrate digestion and fermentation of nutrients, which has a direct impact on animal sustainability and productivity. It is further known that diet composition has an impact on rumen microbial communities, while the proportional roles of feed types and rumen fraction type (solid vs. liquid) to the diversity of bacterial communities in sheep kept indoors are still lacking. This study examined the impact of rumen sample fractions (solid vs. liquid) and diet composition (single vs. mixed) on the diversity and structure of the sheep's rumen bacterial community. METHODS: Eight adult sheep were used in two different feeding groups: mixed feeding (hay, straw, and silage) and single feeding (orchard grass silage only). The solid and liquid fractions of the rumen were separated after 21 days of feeding. The V4 region of the 16 S rRNA gene was sequenced using the Illumina MiSeq platform after microbial DNA was extracted from both fractions. The SILVA database was used to assign amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) for bioinformatic analysis, which was carried out using QIIME2. Using R, analyses of differential abundance, beta diversity, and alpha diversity were performed. RESULTS: While microbial richness stayed consistent across diets (P = 0.065), mixed feeding increased species richness compared to single feeding (P = 0.0076. On the other hand, the rumen sample fraction had a greater impact on microbial community structure: liquid fractions were dominated by taxa linked to fermentation of soluble carbohydrates, while solid fractions showed greater richness (P = 0.012) and were enriched with bacteria associated with fibre (P< 0.001). Significant compositional differences between solid and liquid fractions were found via beta-diversity analysis (PERMANOVA, R² = 0.553, P < 0.001), but remained similar across the feeding regimens (R² = 0.139, P = 0.099). The phyla Bacteroidota (54.82%) and Bacillota (19.17%) dominated the rumen microbiota in all samples, with Prevotella being the most prevalent genus (18.74%). Dietary differences in volatile fatty acid profiles were negligible, suggesting functional redundancy in spite of taxonomic changes in the rumen bacterial community. CONCLUSION: Under the conditions examined, this study shows that the rumen sample fraction (solid vs. liquid) is a more important determinant of the composition of the microbial community than the effects of diet composition. Microbial richness is increased by mixed feeding, while different and functionally complementary bacterial communities are present in solid and liquid rumen fractions. These results emphasize how crucial it is to include both rumen sample fractions in microbiome research and offer insightful information for the improvement of feeding practices or sudden dietary changes meant to enhance nutrient utilization in sheep under indoor conditions.

papers.abstract_en: Bacteria and eukaryotes are integral to the ecological functioning of river systems, while little is known about the spatial patterns and driving mechanisms of different abundance taxa in karst mountainous rivers. The 16S and 18S rRNA amplicon sequencing was used to examine microbial community composition and assembly processes in the surface water of the Tongzi River. The results showed that the community compositions of total and abundant bacteria and eukaryotes formed distinct clusters according to their geographic areas. Similar pattern of community composition was observed in total and abundant taxa. Co-occurrence networks incorporated most abundant taxa and the node-level topological properties of abundant taxa in both bacterial and eukaryotic networks were significantly higher than those of rare taxa. The keystone taxa identified by Zi/Pi analysis were both belonged to abundant taxa. Overall, these findings indicated that the bacterial and eukaryotic community structure and distribution were primarily governed by abundant taxa. Abundant taxa were more strongly influenced by spatial variation than rare taxa. Stochastic processes dominated the assembly of both bacterial and eukaryotic communities. Among the environmental factors analyzed, Oxidation-Reduction Potential (ORP) was the most important factor influencing the bacterial and eukaryotic communities. Furthermore, eukaryotic communities were more sensitive to environmental variations than bacterial communities. The results expand our understanding of the importance of abundant taxa in microbial community assembly in the karst mountainous river.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bacteriophage carry-over, the continued lytic activity of residual phages after experimental sampling, poses a significant challenge in bacteriophage research, potentially skewing experimental results, particularly in the context of preclinical studies where perceived laboratory success may not translate clinically. These inaccuracies, relevant across various bacterial species, underscore the necessity for robust mitigation strategies. This study provides an overview of strategies to mitigate phage carry-over, evaluating their performance on a combination of three mycobacteriophages with lytic activity against M. tuberculosis. RESULTS: We investigated three inactivation methods, including ferrous ammonium sulfate (FAS) and citrate for in vitro applications and N-acetyl-L-cysteine-sodium hydroxide (NALC-NaOH) for sputum decontamination. The citrate buffer offered limited and specific phage inactivation, but FAS was effective in inactivating all three mycobacteriophages (FionnbharthΔ45Δ47, Muddy HRMN0157-2, and Fred313cpm-1Δ33). With pH adapted to 5.0, FAS did not significantly reduce M. tuberculosis H37Rv viability after five minutes exposure. Phage carry-over was determined to be phage-dependent; FionnbharthΔ45Δ47 exhibited the most significant reduction in M. smegmatis colony forming units without phage inactivation measures. Furthermore, we showed that NALC-NaOH methods, commonly used for sputum decontamination, are highly effective in reducing phage titers in aqueous solutions and human sputum samples. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the heterogenous and phage-dependent efficacy of available inactivation buffers, underscoring the critical necessity for researchers to empirically screen their specific phage isolates against chosen inactivation methods. This is crucial to ensure that observed antibacterial effects are correctly attributed to phage activity during the experimental period, rather than to uncontrolled phage carry-over, thereby enhancing the reliability and interpretability of results.

papers.abstract_en: Extracellular high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) serves as a key damage-associated molecular pattern that drives the pathological process of inflammatory liver injury; however, its role in liver fibrosis and the underlying mechanisms need to be elucidated. To investigate the proinflammatory and profibrotic roles of extracellular HMGB1, we used an adenovirus-mediated system to measure HMGB1 secretion in mice. We subsequently constructed two recombinant proteins, PfTrx-HMGB117(95 - 111) and HBcΔ-HMGB134(150 - 183), targeting the interactions of HMGB1 with its receptors, namely, toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE), respectively. Mice were immunized with the two recombinant proteins to assess neutralizing antibody induction and the protective effects of the HMGB1 vaccines against carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced liver fibrosis. Our results revealed the nucleocytoplasmic translocation of HMGB1 in the livers of both humans and mice with fibrosis. Extracellular HMGB1 induced liver inflammation and fibrogenesis in mice. Immunization with the two HMGB1 vaccines resulted in the production of high levels of anti-HMGB1 neutralizing antibodies, which inhibited the activation of hepatic stellate cells (LX-2) and the production of proinflammatory and profibrotic factors in RAW 264.7 cells. Furthermore, vaccination with these compounds significantly protected against CCl4-induced liver injury, inflammation, and fibrosis in mice. These findings demonstrate that extracellular HMGB1, by binding to TLR4 or RAGE, is pivotal in driving liver inflammation and fibrosis. Vaccination against HMGB1 through disruption of interaction with TLR4 or RAGE represents a promising therapeutic strategy for hepatic fibrosis.

These findings underscore the role of farm environments as reservoirs for ARGs and highlight the need for enhanced surveillance, ongoing monitoring, stricter antibiotic policies, and infection control measures to prevent the spread of resistant E. coli isolates and can further reduce resistance risks.

papers.abstract_en: The majority of emerging infectious diseases are zoonotic, having their origin in wildlife before spilling over into the human population. While small mammals are recognized as critical reservoirs for these viruses, their viral diversity remains largely uncharacterized across many African countries. We conducted molecular surveillance of synanthropic rodents and shrews in the Kibera informal settlement in Nairobi and the rural Taita Hills region of Kenya to detect and characterize potential zoonotic viruses. Tissue samples from 228 rodents and shrews were screened for six viral families using PCR assays. Rat hepatitis E virus (HEV) (Rocahepevirus ratti), a rodent-associated virus with potential for human spillover, was identified in Mus musculus and Rattus norvegicus from Kibera. NGS was conducted for the HEV positive samples, and we obtained two near-complete HEV genomes from Rattus norvegicus, which clustered within rodent-associated HEV genotypes in the phylogenetic analysis. The two sequences from the Rattus norvegicus cluster together, indicating a close genetic relationship. Paramyxoviruses belonging to the genera Jeilongvirus and Parahenipavirus were detected both from Taita and Kibera in nine different samples from Rattus norvegicus, Mus minutoides, Crocidura sp and Acomys ignitus. One paramyxovirus positive sample (Acomys ignitus) from Taita was selected for further sequencing with NGS, and a complete genome of a new jeilongvirus was assembled. Phylogenetic analysis of the detected viruses confirmed the close relation to previously known rodent-borne jeilongviruses but also revealed potentially novel jeilong- and parahenipavirus species. Our findings highlight the circulation of potentially zoonotic viruses in both urban and rural small mammals in Kenya. It emphasizes the necessity of continued genomic surveillance of zoonotic viruses to mitigate risks of their spillover into human populations.

papers.abstract_en: Zoonotic diseases pose a significant public health challenge, with most emerging diseases originating from animal populations. In Uganda, Rift Valley fever (RVF), Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF) and brucellosis are endemic, yet critical gaps remain in understanding their transmission dynamics, key vectors and reservoirs, environmental drivers, community knowledge and behaviours and the implementation of One Health policies. The Collaborative One Health Research Initiative on Epidemics-Uganda (COHRIE-Uganda) study developed an integrated, interdisciplinary approach to investigate these diseases across ecologically diverse areas characterised by intense human-livestock-wildlife interaction. The study methodology comprised sequential cross-sectional surveys combining quantitative and qualitative methods, involving community members, livestock, wildlife and vectors across six conservation areas in Uganda. Household surveys and blood sampling were obtained from 3018 individuals and 35 focus group discussions were conducted across 96 villages. 67 in-depth interviews with community leaders and 26 interviews with national policymakers were conducted to evaluate One Health policy implementation. Livestock practices were assessed through farmer questionnaires and blood sampling of 2199 cattle, 343 sheep, 78 pigs and 1582 goats. Invertebrate vector sampling was undertaken of 72,744 mosquitoes and 9273 ticks on livestock hosts with vertebrate host sampling of 612 small mammals. 233 large wildlife were sampled by blood and nasal swabs. Real-time monitoring and detection of zoonotic outbreaks was provided by 127 trained Community One Health Volunteers embedded at each site. COHRIE-Uganda presents a novel interdisciplinary methodology to study zoonotic disease, applying a One Health approach integrating molecular epidemiology, ecology, social sciences and community participatory methods involving humans, livestock, vectors, and wildlife to inform culturally sensitive zoonotic disease interventions.
